critiques.weaknesses: In a game, tapping a piece means 'select to move'; 'tap a piece to ask' collides with that grammar. Chips plus a bubble plus the board at 400 px only fit if the bubble overlays the board edge. `searchmoves` for the piece's moves is another search shape in the queue.
critiques.what_i_would_add: An input rule: the first tap selects and shows legal dots, a second tap on the already-selected piece opens the chips; and one `bubble` component anchored to the board edge that is the only text surface for chips, holds and the coach, so two bubbles can never be live.

critiques.strengths: The tightest verb list: Show me (a 2-ply ghost capture and revert, no words), Take it back, Play it anyway, But... The '-2' float is a tiny element; the ghost capture is one playLine on the ghost layer; Claude only on explicit taps; the end card is two numbers in localStorage.
critiques.weaknesses: 'go depth 10 with multipv set to all legal moves' during think time costs roughly N times a single search; thirty lines is 2-3 s on a phone and will rarely finish before he moves. 'But...' is a text box: the keyboard shifts the layout. 'Tap any enemy piece to see what guards it' collides with selection again.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Replace the all-moves pre-search with `go depth 12 multipv 2` plus one post-drop `go depth 10`, and implement the '-2' float and the ghost capture as the same ghost.playLine every concept's Show me uses.

critiques.strengths: The rewind animation is the history cursor stepping backward with the piece layer's transitions, free once replay exists; 'Play from here' is a load of (fen, history) into the normal loop; the question is a tap graded by chess.js.
critiques.weaknesses: Scoring forty positions at depth 14 is 30-60 s on a phone; a seed game is needed for day one; 'Play from here' needs the opponent engine while the scoring job may still own the worker.
critiques.what_i_would_add: A priority scheduler in engine.js where a user move's search pre-empts the background trace and the trace resumes afterwards, so 'Play from here' is instant even with the trace unfinished.

critiques.strengths: The cheapest page to build and test: six data positions, tap-to-answer, a ghost line, URL-hash sharing, no opponent, Claude only for typed answers; the depth-16 confirmation at load runs in the background and gates the reveal; a shared link needs no Claude.
critiques.weaknesses: The URL hash carries question text, so a tampered link can put arbitrary text on screen; it must be rendered with textContent only. The daily and streak logic is per-browser. The acceptable-reply set must ship in the data. It is a feature, not the product, on day one.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Hash hygiene: a versioned, length-capped schema (#v1&fen=...&q=...) parsed with URLSearchParams, the FEN validated through chess.js, squares through a regex, text via textContent, and a fallback to today's seed when anything fails.

critiques.strengths: The hold ring drawn from chess.js attackers and defenders on drop is the lightest-latency hold of all (under a millisecond, no engine wait). The chip is on tap only. The ring size is one CSS variable from the store.
critiques.weaknesses: A one-second hold on every move is a tax on every move. If 'shows their chair' means a flip per move it is disorienting and heavy; if it means the pulse under the attacker it is fine. The bot sampler (MultiPV 8 at depth 12 with take-material, never-hang-queen, hang-a-minor-at-10% rules) is real JS over info lines and a day of tuning on its own; the self-play tuning is outside any MVP. The depth-3 mate probe is one more search per move. The end card's board is a second instance.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Two tiers in code for the hold: the instant chess.js tier draws the pulse at drop time, the engine tier confirms before the ring completes and clears the pulse when the engine likes the sacrifice, so the ring never waits on the worker.

critiques.strengths: The swap is a flip plus an input lock on the other colour plus a chess.js capture check; the edge count is one number; the trigger is the same gate every Hold concept uses.
critiques.weaknesses: Rotating the board three to six times a game is the heaviest motion of any concept. The flip must wait for the engine verdict (~300 ms after the drop) so a sound sacrifice does not trigger it, which is the pending-state issue again. Taking 'with your own finger' means the input layer accepts the opponent's colour in the swap state.
critiques.what_i_would_add: A `side` input policy in board.js (own, other, none) set by game state, so the swap, the playground and the punishing chair share one pickup rule, and the flip is driven by the same piece-translate mapping with reduced-motion snapping.

critiques.strengths: Entirely chess.js-graded; a data-file corpus; no opponent; verification at authoring time; the grid share is a string; the smallest Claude footprint of the set.
critiques.weaknesses: Thirty verified positions is an authoring job the page cannot do; the three sequential tap-questions with rings are a small state machine; the full answer sets must ship in the data for 'any correct square'. Not the product on day one.
critiques.what_i_would_add: A build script (node plus chess.js, in scripts/, not in the page) that precomputes the three answer sets per position into app/data so the page never derives truth tables at load and the test fixture equals the shipped data.

critiques.concept: Say It Before You Move (market skeptic)
critiques.strengths: The strongest grounding contract: facts by id, a validator that rejects unknown ids and unlisted squares, the template fallback for the top fact. The move always plays immediately and the coach line arrives after, so no hover state is needed; it is the easiest coach to build. A fixed opening position with a known planted threat gives a deterministic first frame.
critiques.weaknesses: A text input on every move at 400 px: the keyboard covers the board. The planted-blunder bot needs up to N verification searches per plant and needs a cap. The faint move list above the board is a move list. The listening pulse plus a 1-4 s call after every Move press is a rhythm the sample contract does not guarantee.
critiques.what_i_would_add: A bottom sheet for the sentence that keeps the top of the board visible, with the board scaled by a CSS variable set from visualViewport.height while the keyboard is open, and the OS dictation key treated as the primary way to 'say it' on a phone.

critiques.strengths: Ghost-move commit with explicit buttons is the most honest UI for verdict latency. The ration is a number; refunds come from the engine; the flip is on demand (three a game), so motion is bounded.
critiques.weaknesses: Flip plus ghost plies on the flipped board at 400 px combines the two hardest board features. Two buttons under the board on every move make every move a two-step unless drag commits directly. The template path carries most looks, as admitted.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Make 'Play it' implicit: a drop commits after a 600 ms ring unless 'Their chair' is tapped inside it, and a drag-and-hold on the destination opens the chair directly, so the common move stays one gesture.

critiques.strengths: The whisper is zero-Claude, pure chess.js precondition matching, instant and fixture-testable; the five-label validator is simple; the placement positions are already verified in the repo.
critiques.weaknesses: A layer over Say It. The persistence story is the feature, and localStorage dies between his laptop and phone; db.d.ts says outside viewers on a public link never write, so db works for Sambudh as owner and the friend's copy stays per-browser. The post-game default-tier call must be cancelable and resumable.
critiques.what_i_would_add: store.js writing habits to data/users/{self}/habits with a localStorage mirror, where the whisper matcher reads an in-memory snapshot loaded once, never the db inside the move handler, so a whisper never waits on a network read.

critiques.strengths: My own: the module seams, the piece layer with transform-translate, pointer events in one path, the two-slot queue, the test plan through __app and the existing stub, and the cut list.
critiques.weaknesses: 'Why?' with three tools (highlight, arrow, evaluate) is two rounds, 2-3 s on quick plus the consent dialog on the first; evaluate lets Claude request a search while the opponent search is queued, so it depends on the queue priorities I only described in Show Me. I under-specified the pending state between landing and verdict.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The pending state and search ids described above, and a rule that day one ships the hold question and the end note only; the Why tool call waits for iteration two.

critiques.strengths: Tools grounded by a page-side guard that refuses to show a losing line as good; ghost.js runs from a scratch Chess so the real position is never touched; one function rewinds on Stop, on signal, on any tap.
critiques.weaknesses: Four quick rounds is 4-6 s; chips collide with selection; busy at 400 px without dimming the real layer.

merged_proposal.name: Hold On
merged_proposal.one_liner: You play a real game against a soft Stockfish; when a move would give a piece away, it lands but does not commit: the board holds it, asks one question you answer by tapping a square, lets you watch the punishment as ghosts, and lets you take it back with no mark against you.
merged_proposal.the_new_interaction: The pending move. On every other board in the world a move is either played or not; here a dropped piece slides to its square (150 ms) and sits in a `pending` state for the ~300 ms the engine needs, and when the move hands over material it becomes `held`: the piece dims to 60%, a small 'Hold on.' chip appears, the two or three squares that matter pulse, and one line in the coach's serif voice asks a question the page already knows the answer to ('Hold on. The knight is about to sit on e5. What defends that square?'). The player answers with his thumb, not a keyboard: a tap on d6 gets 'Yes, the d6 pawn. A knight for a pawn. Take it back?'; a tap on c6 gets 'The c6 knight does guard e5. Is that the only defender? Look at the pawns.' Three verbs sit in the action bar: Show me (the refutation plays as translucent ghosts, 7.Nxe5 dxe5, a small '-2' floats up, then everything slides back), Take it back (the piece slides home, nothing recorded against him), Play it anyway (the opponent punishes every time, one sentence: 'That's the one. Knight for pawn. Now you've felt it.'). On the ninety percent of moves that do not matter nothing is said, nothing is drawn, no eval bar, no move list, no labels; silence is the reward. It is not a chatbot next to a board because there is no text box; Claude speaks exactly one question and one follow-up, inside the hold, grounded by facts the engine and chess.js computed first and validated on the way back, and the whole thing plays identically with Claude absent. Combined from: the designer's visual spec and consent sequencing, the chess coach's gate rules and beat budget, the beginner's four verbs and Show me, the LLM engineer's fact sheet and validator, the game designer's instant chess.js tier for the pulse, and my pending-move state and engine queue.
merged_proposal.core_loop: First thirty seconds: the page opens on a board, white at the bottom, the tournament look (buff and sage squares, hand-drawn SVG silhouettes), one serif line above it: 'Your move. I'll stay quiet unless it matters.' and a small 'Black: beginner' badge; the 7 MB engine warms in a Worker behind the board and the first two Black replies come from a tiny opening book so the player never waits on it. He taps e2, the pawn lifts (scale 1.08, soft shadow), dots appear on e3 and e4, he taps e4, Black's e5 slides in. 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d3: silence. Game one follows the scripted beginner tree out of 1.e4 so something hangs by move five (4...Nxe4?!); he reaches for 5.Nc3, the knight lands, dims, 'Hold on. Their knight just took on e4. What can you take?' He taps e4: 'The d3 pawn takes it. A knight for a pawn. Take it back?' He taps Take it back, plays 5.dxe4, 'That's it.' and the board goes quiet. The loop, with the engine schedule that makes it feel instant: (1) IDLE, player to move: engine.js runs `go depth 12 multipv 2` on the current FEN (search id k) as the pre-search; evalBefore and the best move stream in. (2) pointerdown on an own piece: lift, legal dots from chess.js moves({verbose:true}); tap-tap is the primary path, drag with setPointerCapture and touch-action:none on the board only is the enhancement; a pointerup within 8 px and 300 ms is a tap; promotion is a four-button strip over the target file with Enter and Escape. (3) Drop on a legal square: the piece slides 150 ms and enters `pending` (full opacity, input locked, nothing drawn); chess.js computes the post-move facts synchronously (attackers and defenders per square, pieces of his now attacked and undefended or attacked by a cheaper piece, free captures he ignored, checks and mate-in-one for the opponent); engine.js sends `stop`, discards the pre-search's late bestmove by id, and runs `go depth 10` on the post-move FEN (id k+1), ~0.3 s. (4) Verdict in gate.js, a pure function: cpLoss = evalBefore from his side minus evalAfter from his side; HOLD when cpLoss >= 200 AND chess.js can name the mechanism AND the engine's reply is a capture, a check or mate AND he is not already five points down AND he has pressed Play it anyway fewer than twice this game; mate-in-one allowed or missed always holds; a positional loss never holds. (5) Clean: commit, last-move tint, `setoption name Skill Level value 2` then `go depth 6` (id k+2) for the opponent's reply, slide, back to IDLE with a fresh pre-search. (6) Held: the board root gets data-hold, the piece dims, the pulse set is drawn, the template question from gate.js shows at once, and coach.js fires one quick-tier sample.json call with a fresh AbortController; the input mode becomes 'answer' (taps are graded against the answer-square set from chess.js, never from Claude). Claude's question replaces the template only if it arrives within 2.5 s and no tap has happened. (7) Show me: ghost.js plays the refutation (2 plies, 600 ms apart, '-N' float) from a scratch Chess on the 50%-opacity ghost layer while the real layer dims to 35%, then rewinds; aborts and rewinds on any pointerdown. (8) Take it back: the piece slides home, the controller aborts, the hold is logged {fen, san, look, outcome:'back', taps}, the cached pre-search is reused, IDLE. Play it anyway: commit; the opponent plays the engine's true best reply (Skill Level 20 for this one move) so the punishment is certain; one sentence; logged. (9) Game over on chess.js isGameOver, or the bot resigns when nine or more points of material down for three moves so games end; the end screen shows '0 pieces given away. Two holds, both taken back.', each hold as a small static board (board.js in static mode), and one 'Again' button; the holds go to store.js. (10) Next game opens with one line that names the thing ('Watch the pawns today.') from the stored categories, no Claude needed.
merged_proposal.mvp_slice: One page, no build step, served by python3 -m http.server and published with `files`: app/index.html (title, tokens on :root, dark via prefers-color-scheme guarded by :root:not([data-theme="light"]) and again under :root[data-theme="dark"], explicit body background, the twelve piece <symbol>s inline, Google Fonts Source Serif 4 and IBM Plex Sans with fallbacks), app/styles.css, app/src/main.js (one state object, render(state) after every mutation), board.js (a static 64-cell CSS grid of squares; a piece layer where each piece is a focusable <button class=pc data-square> placed by transform: translate(calc(var(--f)*100%), calc(var(--r)*100%)) with a 150 ms transition that prefers-reduced-motion sets to 0; the file/rank mapping honours a flip flag from day one even though Black is not playable yet; overlay layers for last-move tint, legal dots and the hold pulse; one SVG for arrows; a static mode for the end screen's small boards), input.js (pointer events only, tap-tap primary, drag enhancement, promotion strip, a `side` policy for which colour may be picked up, an 'answer' mode where taps grade instead of move), game.js (chess.js 1.4.0 wrapper, history, load(fen) for tests), engine.js (the Worker, a serialized UCI queue with search ids, stop-then-go, info-line parser for multipv scores and pv, a search(fen, {depth, multipv, skill}) promise, a warm-up promise, a tiny book in data/openings.json for the first replies and the game-one scripted tree), facts.js (the chess.js fact sheet every concept shares: attackers, defenders, hanging, free captures, checks, mate-in-one), gate.js (the pure verdict function and the template copy), ghost.js (playLine on the ghost layer from a scratch Chess, rewind on abort or any tap), coach.js (sample resolved as window.__stubSample ?? await window.claude?.use?.('sample'); one prompt builder for the hold question returning {question, answer_squares, if_right, if_wrong}; the validator: every square a real square and a subset of the chess.js answer set, no answer square named inside the question, no SAN token outside the listed moves, else the template stands; error codes: not_granted, sampling_disabled, not_declared and capability_disabled set a flag and never call again; rate_limited skips Claude for the next three holds; invalid_json, refused, empty_completion fall back for this hold; cancelled shows nothing; a fresh AbortController per call aborted by Take it back and Play it anyway), store.js ({get, set, append, list} on localStorage for the MVP, with the db path data/users/{self}/holds reserved and the owner-only write rule from db.d.ts noted for iteration two), ui.js (the 44 px header, the serif caption clamped to three lines with fixed height so the board never jumps, the board at min(100vw - 32px, 62vh), a sticky 56 px action bar with the one primary action, keyboard focus visible). Claude in the slice: the hold question only, quick tier, sample.json, stubbed in tests. Acceptance in scripts/app_check.js scenarios, all from verified lesson positions and driven through window.__app = {load(fen), play(san), fen(), state(), waitEngine(), holds()}: the Italian after 6...d6 (r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/4p3/2B1P3/2NP1N2/PPP2PPP/R1BQ1RK1 w - - 0 7), play Nxe5 and assert [data-hold], pulse set {e5, d6}, template text visible and exactly one sample call with modelTier quick; tap d6 and assert the 'Yes' copy; Show me and assert the ghost layer moved twice and fen() is unchanged; Take it back and assert fen() is the original and the controller aborted; Bxf7+ also holds; h3 passes in silence and Black replies; the Ruy after 3...a6: O-O holds, Ba4 passes; the Scholar's position after 3.Bc4: ...Nf6 holds (mate in one allowed); a window.__stubReplies entry naming an off-list square leaves the template on screen; a clean six-move sequence makes zero sample calls; the four screenshots (desktop and 400 px, light and dark) show no horizontal overflow and no console errors. Build order for the day: board and pieces, input, game, engine queue and opponent, facts and gate with the pending and held states and the three verbs, ghost Show me, coach with validator and stub, end screen and store, themes and phone and reduced motion, scenarios and screenshots. Explicitly cut from day one (too ambitious for one page in one day, and each is a seam, not a rewrite): playing Black and the flip animation (the mapping is flip-ready), db plus user (behind store.js), any tool-bearing call (Why?, Show-me-with-words), the typed 'But...', the post-game default-tier review, the bot sampler and its tuning (fixed Skill Level 2, punish-always rule), PGN paste or download, share links, piece chips, sound. Licensing flagged: Stockfish GPLv3 means the page's own source should be GPL-compatible; the piece silhouettes are drawn by us so there is no third licence.
merged_proposal.why_this_wins: On novelty it is the one interaction none of the incumbents has: a move that lands but does not commit, a question answered on the squares, and a take-back with no shame, all before the blunder exists. On beginner value it holds only what loses games under 1000 (a piece given to a one-move look, a free piece ignored, a mate in one) and says nothing otherwise, which is the chess coach's band belief encoded as a rule the tests can enforce. On feasibility it is the only concept where the engine's hard real-time job (a verdict in ~300 ms) is solved by a schedule rather than hoped for: pre-search while he thinks, one post-drop search, search ids so the single-threaded worker never plays a stale bestmove, and a pending state that makes the latency honest on a slow phone; the gate and the facts are pure functions, the board is one piece layer animated by transform, and every flow is assertable in headless Chromium through the stub app_check.js already installs. On cost it spends zero Claude calls in a clean game and one quick call per hold, each cancelable and each validated against chess.js before it touches the board, so Claude can never be wrong about chess and its absence is invisible. On delight it is the piece that will not land, the ghost capture he watches on his own board, and the silence on the move after he takes it back. Every other concept on the table (the chair swap, the chips, the daily, the habits, the post-game review) is a policy or a page that plugs into the same pending state, fact sheet, engine queue, ghost layer and store, so shipping this first buys the seams the rest of them need.

spec.tagline: Chess that catches your hand before the piece is gone.
spec.thesis: Under 1000 a game is decided in the half-second before a piece lands on a square where it can be taken, and nothing in the world acts in that half-second the way a coach does: by stopping the hand and asking a question. The incumbents that interrupt (Chessmaster's Blunder Alert, Fritz's coach, HIARCS, Lucas Chess, Chess.com Play Coach) tell you the move was bad or show you a better one; the review products (Game Review, Lichess Learn, Chessiro, ChessGPT) explain afterwards; the chat-with-an-engine apps make you ask. Hold On is a real game against an opponent that plays like an 800 (it leaves pieces for you and always takes yours) in which a move that would give material away does not land: the piece lifts, the square goes amber, and one line asks a question you answer by tapping the board: 'Hold on. If the knight lands there, what takes it? Tap it.' You take it back with no mark against you, or play it anyway and feel it, or press 'But...' and argue your plan in your own words, and the coach answers your plan with a question, never a move. The engine and chess.js decide everything that is chess, instantly and before Claude is asked; Claude does only what a template cannot: put the question in this player's words for this exact position, and read a beginner's belief ('I'm attacking his king') and find what is false in it. On the ninety percent of moves that do not matter it says nothing, which is the only reason it can be believed when it speaks. It should exist because it is the first chess software whose coaching happens where the rating is actually lost, in the player's hand, and because it is buildable in a day: one page, an engine in a Worker, two quick Claude calls sharing one fact sheet and one validator, fully playable without Claude, and testable in headless Chromium from positions already verified at depth 20 in this repo.
spec.the_new_interaction: The held move that asks, and that you can argue with. You drop a piece. Most of the time it lands and the opponent replies inside a second with nothing said. When the engine finds that this move hands over material to a one-move reply (a piece left where a pawn or a cheaper piece takes it, a free piece of theirs walked past, a mate in one allowed or missed), the piece does not land: it stays lifted over the destination with a soft shadow, that square breathes amber, every other square dims one shade, and the serif line above the board asks one question whose answer is a square: 'Hold on. If the knight lands there, what takes it? Tap it.' Nothing on the board is marked, so the look is his to do. He answers with his thumb. chess.js already holds the right squares, so the tap is graded instantly: 'Yes, the pawn. A knight for a pawn.' or 'The knight on c6 could too. Is there something cheaper? Look at the pawns.' or 'Not that one. Look at the pawns next to the square.' (one retry, then the taker glows). Then he decides: 'Take it back' slides the piece home and nothing is recorded against him; 'Play it anyway' commits, the opponent takes every time, one sentence ('There it goes. A knight for a pawn. You saw it coming; that counts.'), and that piece on that square is never held again this game; 'Show me' plays the capture as a ghost, a small '-2' floats off his side of the board, a beat, and everything slides back. And 'But...': the only text field in the product, which exists only inside a hold. He types 'I'm attacking his king' and the coach answers his plan, not a number: 'You are, and the bishop on c4 already points at f7. But it is their move first, and the pawn on d6 takes the knight before you get there. Is there a square that still looks at their king that no pawn can reach?' with d6 and e5 lit. One reply, no thread. Three things make this not a chatbot next to a board and not Fritz on a web page: the coach never names the move and never names the answer square, it speaks only inside a hold the engine decided, and the answer to its question is a tap on the board. Every chess fact in every sentence was computed by chess.js and Stockfish before Claude was asked and is checked again on the way out; a wrong square can never reach the board.
spec.target_user: Sambudh first: played before, rating once under 1000 and forgotten, has studied nothing, opens 1.e4, loses to pieces taken for free and one-move threats, has a phone in one hand and ten to fifteen minutes, and has closed every app that showed him an evaluation bar or a red '??'. Then everyone like him: adult returners and late beginners under about 1000 who want to play rather than read, who know how the pieces move and would never open a lesson. Not titled players, not puzzle grinders, not children who cannot read a sentence. He is the first tester, so the first game is designed to show the product working within fifteen seconds without a manual.
spec.first_30_seconds: 0 s: the page opens on a tournament board (buff and green squares, hand-drawn pieces), White at the bottom, not on the start position but on the Italian after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 (FEN r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/2B1P3/5N2/PPPP1PPP/RNBQK2R w KQkq - 4 4, verified in lesson 0001 at depth 20). One serif line above it: 'Your move. Most people take on f7 here. Go on.' Below the board an empty action bar. No menu, no eval bar, no move list, no rating, no text box. The 7 MB engine is warming in a Worker behind the board; he never waits on it. 3-8 s: he taps the c4 bishop (it lifts a little, legal squares show as faint dots, f7 as a ring because it is a capture), taps f7. The bishop slides to f7 in 150 ms and stays lifted with a shadow; f7 breathes amber; the rest of the board dims; the line reads 'Hold on. If the bishop takes there, what takes it back? Tap it.' This hold is canned (the position is verified, the answer set is {e8}); no Claude call, no consent dialog yet. 8-14 s: he looks, taps the black king on e8. 'Yes, the king. A bishop for a pawn.' The action bar now holds [Take it back] (ink, primary) and [Play it anyway] (quiet); under the line, two small links: 'Show me' and 'But...'. 14-19 s: he taps 'Show me'. The ghost king slides to f7 and takes, a small amber '-2' floats up from his edge of the board, a beat, and the bishop and king slide back to where they were. No words. 19-24 s: he taps 'Take it back'. The bishop floats home to c4. The line: 'Good. That is all I do: I hold the move, I ask, you decide. Now a real game.' 24-30 s: the board resets to the start position, the line reads 'Your move.', he plays 1.e4 (tap e2, tap e4), Black's 1...e5 slides in from the opening book in under half a second, and the page goes quiet. (If he instead played 4.Nxe5 at step 3 the same hold fires with answer set {c6}; if he played a safe move like 4.d3 the line says 'Safe. Now try the one everyone plays: bishop takes f7.' and the move slides back; if he tapped 'Play it anyway' the king takes the bishop for real, the '-2' floats, the line says 'Now you have felt it. Here is a real game.', and the board resets. Every path reaches the real game in under 45 s with both buttons understood.)
core_loop: 1. 'Your move.' While he thinks, the Worker is already searching his position (depth 12, multipv 2) so the best move, its evaluation, any free capture available to him and any mate in one for him are known before he touches a piece.

2. He moves by tap-tap (primary) or drag (enhancement): the piece lifts, legal squares show as dots and captures as rings; on the drop the piece slides 150 ms and enters a pending state (full opacity, input locked, nothing drawn). chess.js builds the post-move fact sheet synchronously; the engine stops the pre-search (its late bestmove is discarded by search id) and runs depth 10 on the new position, about 0.3 s.

3. Clean (cp loss under 200, or no mechanism chess.js can name): the move commits, the last-move tint appears, the opponent replies inside a second with a 150 ms slide, nothing is said. If his move captured a piece the engine and chess.js both called free: a green ring on the square for a beat and 'Free knight. You looked.' If their last move attacked a piece of his and his move saved it: a one-word grey chip under the line, 'Looked.'

4. Hold: the gate fires only for the four shapes that lose games under 1000, in this priority: (a) his move allows a mate in one; (b) his move leaves a piece of his where a capture takes it for a net loss of two or more (attacked and undefended, or attacked by a pawn or cheaper piece; cp loss 200 or more at depth 10; the engine's reply is that capture); (c) the same, but the piece was already attacked by their last move and he moved something else; (d) he had a mate in one or a free capture worth two or more (the pre-search's best move is that capture, chess.js confirms the target was free) and played something else losing 200 or more. A positional loss of any size never holds. The piece stays lifted, the square breathes amber, the board dims, and the template question for the category appears at once: (a) 'Hold on. Checks. Where does their queen land? Tap it.' (b) 'Hold on. If the knight lands there, what takes it? Tap it.' or, for a capture of a defended piece, 'Hold on. Before you take there: what takes back? Tap it.' (c) 'Hold on. Their last move reached one of yours. Tap it.' (d) 'Hold on. Something of theirs is free right now. Tap it.' or 'Hold on. You have a checkmate on the board. Tap the square.' In the same handler one quick-tier Claude call (K1) is fired with a fresh AbortController; its validated question replaces the template with a 120 ms cross-fade only if it arrives before his first tap and the hold is still open.

5. He answers by tapping a square. chess.js grades against its own answer set, never Claude's: right ('Yes, the pawn. A knight for a pawn.'), partial (another legitimate taker: 'The knight on c6 could too. Is there something cheaper? Look at the pawns.'), wrong (one hint: 'Not that one. Look at the pawns next to the square.'; after a second wrong tap the answer square glows and the line names it in piece words). The action bar shows [Take it back] [Play it anyway]; two text links under the line: 'Show me' and 'But...'.

6. 'Show me': the engine's own refutation (one or two plies) plays as translucent ghosts on a second piece layer while the real pieces dim to 35 percent; a '-N' in piece points floats off his edge of the board; a beat; everything slides back. No words, no Claude. Any tap aborts and rewinds it.

7. 'But...': a one-line field opens in the action bar ('Say what you were going for'; the OS keyboard's mic is dictation for free; the board scales down with visualViewport so the held piece stays visible). On send the field closes, the line pulses 'Looking...', and one quick-tier call (K2) returns two sentences that acknowledge his plan, state the one fact that breaks it, and end with a question, with up to three squares lit. One reply per hold; then the link is gone. Hidden entirely when Claude is absent or declined.

8. He decides. 'Take it back': the piece slides home, the pre-search result is reused, the line reads 'Your move.' and nothing is recorded against him. 'Play it anyway': the move commits, the opponent plays the engine's true best reply (full strength for this one move) so the punishment is certain, one sentence ('There it goes. A knight for a pawn. You saw it coming; that counts.'), the piece-and-square pair is never held again this game, and after the second play-anyway in a game the coach stays quiet until the close. Either button aborts any pending Claude call. The hold is logged {fen, san, category, taps, outcome}.

9. The opponent (Stockfish in the Worker, depth 8, multipv 6, a weighted pick inside 80 cp of best so it plays like a person at his level): it always plays the top move when that move captures two points or more or mates, so a hung piece is punished every time; the 80 cp window means it never hangs its queen or walks into mate; and between its 5th and 25th moves, roughly one move in eight, it deliberately plays a candidate that leaves a minor piece free, verified by a depth-10 search that his capture really wins 200 cp or more, so he gets to be the one who looks and takes. It resigns when nine or more points down for three of its own moves, so games end: 'Black gives up. You are a queen ahead and it knows it.'

10. Game over (mate, resignation, draw): the line says 'Checkmate. Well played.' or 'That one got away.' and the close card appears under the board in units he can feel: 'Pieces given away: 1 (last game 4). Holds: 3, two taken back. Free pieces taken: 2.' with each hold as a small static board, and one button, [Again]. The counts and holds go to localStorage.

11. The next game opens on the start position with one remembered line built from the stored categories ('Two holds last game, both a pawn you did not see. Watch the pawns.'), zero Claude calls, and the opponent's gift rate steps down only after a game with zero pieces given away.

mvp_features.name: The board
mvp_features.description: A static 64-cell CSS grid of squares under an absolutely positioned piece layer where each piece is a focusable <button class=pc data-square> placed by transform: translate() with a 150 ms transition (0 under prefers-reduced-motion), so moves, take-backs and the future flip animate for free. Twelve hand-drawn SVG piece silhouettes as inline <symbol>s used by <use> (no Unicode glyphs, which are tofu in headless Chromium and look like text on Android; no third-party set, so no licence beside Stockfish's). Pointer events in one path: tap-to-select then tap-to-move is primary; drag with setPointerCapture and touch-action: none on the board is the enhancement; a pointerup within 8 px and 300 ms is a tap. Legal squares as faint dots, captures as rings, last move as a translucent ink tint, coordinates as small letters inside the edge squares. Promotion is a four-button strip over the target file (Enter and Escape bound). The board is min(100vw - 32px, 62vh) with 16 px gutters at 400 px; keyboard focus is visible on every piece and button.
mvp_features.why_mvp: The board is the whole interface; every answer, from the engine or Claude, lands on its squares. Nothing else can be tested or felt until it exists, and the hold's lift, the ghost layer and the take-back slide all come from the same transform-driven piece layer.
mvp_features.acceptance: In scripts/app_check.js at 1280 px and 400 px, light and dark: four screenshots with no horizontal overflow, zero console errors, zero page errors, zero failed requests. document.querySelectorAll('.pc').length === 32 on the start position; every .pc is a button with a visible focus ring when focused via keyboard. A scenario taps .pc[data-square=e2] then the e4 cell and asserts window.__app.fen() begins with 'rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP' and that the e2 piece's transform changed. With page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion: 'reduce'}) the computed transition-duration on .pc is '0s'.

mvp_features.name: The opponent
mvp_features.description: Stockfish 18 lite in one Web Worker behind a serialized UCI queue (uci, isready, setoption, position, go, stop) with search ids so a late bestmove from a stopped search is discarded, never played. The first two Black replies to 1.e4 come from a 20-line opening book (data/book.json: Italian, Ruy, Scholar's defence, Petroff) so the first moves are instant while the WASM warms. Then: go depth 8 multipv 6; candidates within 80 cp of the best; a weighted pick (50/25/12/8/5 percent); forced top move when the top move is a capture gaining 200 cp or more or a mate; the gift rule between its 5th and 25th moves (roughly one in eight, with jitter): choose a candidate after which a bot minor piece is attacked by the player and undefended or attacked by a pawn (chess.js), confirm with a depth-10 search that the player's best reply is that capture and gains 200 cp or more from the player's side, else no gift this move; it resigns when its own evaluation is at or below -900 for three consecutive bot moves. Play-it-anyway replies use the engine's true best move at depth 12.
mvp_features.why_mvp: Every reviewer named the opponent as the hardest engineering and the thing that makes the free-capture look ('what can I take?') get reps at all; Stockfish at a low Skill Level plays alien moves and hangs nothing, which teaches only defence. The punish-always rule is what makes a hold's 'Play it anyway' a lesson rather than a gamble.
mvp_features.acceptance: A scenario plays 1.e4 and asserts Black's reply arrives within 2 s with the line empty; plays the Italian to 3...Nf6 via window.__app.play and asserts Black's moves are legal (chess.js accepts each) and that the position never contains a Black queen attacked and undefended. From the verified position after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d3 Nxe4 (Black has just hung a knight to the player) loaded with the player as Black-to-move disabled, i.e. window.__app.load(fen) with the bot to move: the bot's reply is dxe4 (the forced-capture rule) 10 times out of 10. With window.__app.state().giftDue forced true on a quiet middlegame position, the bot's chosen move leaves a minor piece attacked-and-undefended per chess.js and window.__app.state().lastGift.verified === true, or no gift is recorded. A scripted position with the bot a queen down for three bot moves ends the game with data-state=over and the line containing 'gives up'.

mvp_features.name: The silent gate
mvp_features.description: A pure function verdict(evalBefore, evalAfter, bestReply, factsAfter, factsBefore, preSearchBest) in gate.js. Evaluations are converted to the player's side (Stockfish reports side-to-move; mate N maps to +/-(10000-N)); cpLoss = evalBefore - evalAfter. Categories in priority: allowed_mate (the reply search reports mate 1 against him); hanging_after_move (cpLoss >= 200, the engine's best reply is a capture, chess.js names the captured piece as attacked-and-undefended or attacked by a cheaper piece after his move, net loss >= 2 points); ignored_attack (the same, but chess.js says that piece was already attacked before his move); missed_mate (the pre-search reported mate 1 for him and he played something else); free_piece_ignored (the pre-search's best move is a capture whose target chess.js calls free, worth >= 2 points, and cpLoss >= 200). Suppressed after the second play-anyway of the game and for a piece-and-square pair he already played anyway. Never fires on a positional loss. The engine schedule: pre-search go depth 12 multipv 2 while he thinks; on drop, stop, then go depth 10 on the post-move FEN; the pending state is invisible under 250 ms and shows a faint dot on the piece beyond that.
mvp_features.why_mvp: The gate is the coach's band belief encoded as a rule: under 1000 only material lost to a one-move look matters. A hold that fires on positional losses is a nag by game three, and a gate without the capture-or-mate test holds things a beginner cannot see. Making it a pure function makes it unit-testable without a browser.
mvp_features.acceptance: All from verified positions, via window.__app.load(fen) then window.__app.play(san), asserting document.getElementById('board').dataset.state and dataset.hold: Italian after 6...d6 (r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/4p3/2B1P3/2NP1N2/PPP2PPP/R1BQ1RK1 w - - 0 7): Nxe5 -> held, hold=hanging_after_move; Bxf7+ -> held; h3 -> committed, no hold, Black replies, window.__sampleCalls.length === 0. Italian after 4.d3 Nxe4 (r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/2B1n3/3P1N2/PPP2PPP/RNBQK2R w KQkq - 0 5): Nc3 held with hold=free_piece_ignored; dxe4 committed and the line contains 'You looked'. Placement after 7...O-O (r2q1rk1/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/2b1p3/2B1P1b1/2PP1N1P/PP3PP1/RNBQ1RK1 w - - 1 8): Nbd2 held (free_piece_ignored), hxg4 committed with 'You looked'. After 5...Ng4 (r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1P1n1/3P1N1P/PPP2PP1/RNBQK2R w KQkq - 1 6): O-O held, hxg4 committed. Each verdict arrives within 1.5 s of the drop in headless Chromium.

mvp_features.name: The hold
mvp_features.description: When the gate fires, the board root gets data-state=held and data-hold=<category>; CSS lifts the piece (translateY(-6px) scale(1.06), soft shadow, full opacity), breathes the destination square amber (1.6 s inset glow; a static amber ring under reduced motion), dims the other squares with a 12 percent ink overlay, and swaps the input layer to answer mode (taps grade, nothing moves). The template question for the category appears in the serif line at once; 'Hold on.' is always its first two words. The action bar fills with [Take it back] (ink, primary) and [Play it anyway] (quiet); two text links, 'Show me' and 'But...', sit under the line. The line has a fixed three-line height so the board never jumps.
mvp_features.why_mvp: This is the product: the piece that will not land. It must render instantly from the rule, with no dependency on Claude, or the beat is a stall.
mvp_features.acceptance: After window.__app.play('Nxe5') in the 6...d6 position: #board.dataset.state === 'held', the e5 cell has class 'amber', the moved .pc has class 'lifted' and is positioned at e5, .coach textContent starts with 'Hold on.', buttons [data-action=takeback] and [data-action=anyway] are visible and the first is focused, links [data-action=showme] and [data-action=but] are present, and tapping a piece of his own does not change window.__app.fen(). The template question text contains no square name from window.__app.state().hold.answerSquares.

mvp_features.name: Tap-to-answer
mvp_features.description: In answer mode a tap on any square is graded by chess.js against the hold's answer set (hanging/ignored: the enemy squares that can capture the piece, the cheapest marked best; free_piece_ignored: the free piece's square; allowed_mate and missed_mate: the mating square). Right shows the if_right line and a green ring; a legitimate but not-cheapest taker shows if_partial; a wrong tap shows if_wrong once, and a second wrong tap glows the best answer square and names it in piece words ('The pawn on d6.'). The copy comes from Claude's validated reply if it arrived, else from the template table keyed by category and piece names.
mvp_features.why_mvp: Answering on the board is what turns a warning into a look the player did himself; it is the difference between this and Fritz. The grading must be the page's, not Claude's, so it is never wrong.
mvp_features.acceptance: In the 6...d6 position after Nxe5: window.__app.tap('d6') -> .coach contains 'Yes' and 'pawn', the d6 cell has class 'ok'; reload the position, Nxe5, tap('c6') -> .coach contains 'pawns' (the partial line) and no 'ok' class; tap('a1') -> .coach contains 'Not that one'; tap('a2') -> the d6 cell has class 'ok' and .coach contains 'pawn on d6'. In the Ruy after 3...a6, O-O then tap('b5') is right. After 1.f3 e5, g4 then tap('h4') is right. In the Scholar's position, Qh3 then tap('f7') is right.

mvp_features.name: Show me
mvp_features.description: ghost.js plays the engine's refutation (the capture, and the recapture if the gate's exchange has one) on a second piece layer at 50 percent opacity fed by a scratch Chess instance, 600 ms per ply, while the real layer dims to 35 percent; when the capture lands a serif '-N' (the net loss in piece points) floats up 18 px from the player's board edge over 700 ms and fades; after a 500 ms beat the ghosts slide back and the real layer returns. Any pointerdown, Take it back or Play it anyway aborts and rewinds it. Under reduced motion: the final ghost position is shown statically for 1.2 s with a static '-N' label beside the board.
mvp_features.why_mvp: Four partners named this the best single piece of feedback on the table: a beginner understands minus two before centipawns, and watching the future happen on his own board, then undo itself, is the 'feel why' that no sentence gives. It needs no Claude and no language.
mvp_features.acceptance: In the 6...d6 position after Nxe5: click [data-action=showme]; within 300 ms a .ghost piece exists at e5 belonging to Black; within 1.5 s the float element .loss has text '-2'; after it completes #board.dataset.state === 'held' again, document.querySelectorAll('.ghost').length === 0, and window.__app.fen() is unchanged from before Show me. Clicking [data-action=takeback] during the animation rewinds immediately and restores the pre-move FEN.

mvp_features.name: Take it back and Play it anyway
mvp_features.description: Take it back: the piece slides home (150 ms), the hold closes, the cached pre-search is reused so the next drop is judged without re-searching, the line reads 'Your move.', nothing is counted against him, and the pending Claude controller is aborted. Play it anyway: the move commits, the opponent replies with the engine's true best move at depth 12 (full strength for this one move), one templated sentence names what happened in piece words ('There it goes. A knight for a pawn. You saw it coming; that counts.'), the hold is counted on the close card, that piece-and-square pair is excluded from the gate for the rest of the game, and after the second play-anyway the gate is silent until the close. Both are logged {fen, san, category, taps, outcome}.
mvp_features.why_mvp: The dignified take-back is the emotional thesis in one button; play-it-anyway being real, counted and never nagged is what keeps the coach from becoming a parent's hand on the wrist. The quiet-after-two rule is the anti-nag rule every reviewer asked for.
mvp_features.acceptance: 6...d6 position, Nxe5, [data-action=takeback]: window.__app.fen() equals the loaded FEN, #board.dataset.state === 'idle', .coach text is 'Your move.', window.__app.holds().slice(-1)[0].outcome === 'back', and the stub reports the K1 call as cancelled if it had not resolved. Reload, Nxe5, [data-action=anyway]: Black's reply is dxe5 within 2 s, .coach contains 'knight for a pawn', window.__app.holds().slice(-1)[0].outcome === 'anyway'. A scenario that plays anyway twice in one game then plays Bxf7+ in a later position where it would hold asserts no hold fires (data-state goes pending -> idle).

mvp_features.name: Rewards for the look
mvp_features.description: When his move captures a piece that both chess.js (attacked and undefended, or attacked by a cheaper piece) and the pre-search (best move was that capture) called free: a green ring on the square for 900 ms and the line 'Free knight. You looked.' (piece name from the capture). When their last move newly attacked a piece of his and after his move nothing of his is hanging: a one-word grey chip under the line, 'Looked.', for 1.2 s. Neither involves Claude.
mvp_features.why_mvp: The chess coach and game designer both found the same hole in every hold concept: silence is the right response to a neutral move, not to a good one. The free-capture look is half of what loses games under 1000 and needs a reward or it gets no reps.
mvp_features.acceptance: Italian after 4.d3 Nxe4: window.__app.play('dxe4') -> .coach contains 'You looked', the e4 cell has class 'ok' within 200 ms. Ruy after 3...a6: play('Ba4') -> a .chip element with text 'Looked.' appears within 300 ms and is gone within 2 s. A quiet move in a quiet position (6...d6 position, h3) shows neither.

mvp_features.name: The tutorial hold
mvp_features.description: On first visit (localStorage flag absent) the page opens on the verified Italian after 3...Nf6 with the line 'Your move. Most people take on f7 here. Go on.' The gate runs as normal but the question and follow-ups for this position are canned and no Claude call is made; the answer sets are {e8} for Bxf7+ and {c6} for Nxe5. A safe move slides back with 'Safe. Now try the one everyone plays: bishop takes f7.' Take it back ends with 'Good. That is all I do: I hold the move, I ask, you decide. Now a real game.'; Play it anyway lets the king take, floats the '-2', and ends with 'Now you have felt it. Here is a real game.' Either path resets to the start position and sets the flag.
mvp_features.why_mvp: He must know what a hold is before anything is at stake and before the platform's consent dialog can appear; the product designer's sequencing was the single smartest UX decision in the pile and the whole team adopted it.
mvp_features.acceptance: With localStorage cleared, load the page: window.__app.fen() equals the 3...Nf6 FEN and .coach contains 'Go on'. play('Bxf7+') -> held with window.__sampleCalls.length === 0; tap('e8') -> 'Yes'; [data-action=takeback] -> .coach contains 'real game' and window.__app.fen() is the start position; localStorage.getItem('holdon.v1.tutorialSeen') === '1'. Reloading now opens on the start position with 'Your move.'

mvp_features.name: Claude K1: the question in your words
mvp_features.description: On every real (non-tutorial) hold, coach.js fires sample.json(prompt, {modelTier: 'quick', signal}) with a fresh AbortController, where prompt = one fixed instruction block (with a version tag) plus the fact sheet from facts.js (FEN, side, the held move in words and SAN, what happens if it lands in piece words, the look skipped, the answer squares with the best marked, the allowed squares, the listed moves, this game's holds so far by category and outcome, last game's remembered line). It returns {question, if_right, if_partial, if_wrong}. validate.js accepts it only if: the question is at most 18 words and starts with 'Hold on.' (prepended if missing), no answer square appears in the question, every square named anywhere is in the allowed set, no SAN-shaped token outside the listed moves, no signed number, none of blunder/mistake/inaccuracy/??, follow-ups at most 20 words. Accepted text replaces the template only if the hold is still open and no tap has happened; otherwise it is dropped. sample is resolved as window.__stubSample ?? await window.claude?.use?.('sample'). Error codes: not_granted, sampling_disabled, not_declared, capability_disabled, capability_removed set claudeOff for the view (template everywhere, But... hidden, no message); rate_limited skips Claude for the next three holds; invalid_json, refused, empty_completion, upstream_error fall back to the template for this hold; cancelled shows nothing. Zero calls in a clean game.
mvp_features.why_mvp: The question is the product's voice; templated questions become wallpaper by game five, and only an LLM can choose which look to point at and phrase it for this position and this player's history without naming the answer. It costs one quick call per hold, never blocks the beat, and the page is identical without it.
mvp_features.acceptance: 6...d6 position with window.__stubReplies = ['{"question":"Hold on. If the knight lands there, what takes it? Tap it.","if_right":"Yes, the pawn. A knight for a pawn.","if_partial":"The knight on c6 could too. Look at the pawns.","if_wrong":"Not that one. Look at the pawns next to the square."}']: play('Nxe5') -> window.__sampleCalls.length === 1, __sampleCalls[0].opts.modelTier === 'quick', __sampleCalls[0].opts.tools.length === 0, __sampleCalls[0].input contains the FEN and the string 'd6'; within 1 s .coach text equals the stub question. A second run with a reply whose question contains 'd6' leaves the template on screen and window.__coachRejects === 1. A third with squares ['h8'] in if_wrong is rejected the same way. A reply containing 'blunder' is rejected. A hold followed immediately by Take it back shows the template only and the stub records the call as aborted. With --no-stub (sample absent) the hold, the template, the tap grading, Show me and both buttons behave identically and [data-action=but] is absent.

mvp_features.name: Claude K2: But...
mvp_features.description: Inside a hold, the 'But...' link opens a single-line <input enterkeyhint=done autocomplete=off> in the action bar with placeholder 'Say what you were going for' and a send button; the board scales via a CSS variable set from visualViewport.height so the held piece stays visible with the keyboard open. On send the field closes, the line shows 'Looking...' with a soft pulse, and coach.js fires sample.json(prompt, {modelTier: 'quick', cache: false, signal}) with the same fact sheet plus the player's sentence, asking for {say, squares}: at most two sentences and 45 words; first acknowledge what is true in the plan, then the one fact that breaks it, then end with one question that names no move; plain piece words; up to three squares from the allowed set. validate.js applies the same rules (squares subset, no SAN outside listed moves, no numbers, banned words, ends with a question mark). The reply appears in the line with its squares lit; the link is gone for this hold. The first Claude call of a view may happen here or at K1; either way the held state is stable while the consent dialog is up. Hidden when claudeOff, when sample is null, and for 60 s after rate_limited with the line 'Coach is resting.'
mvp_features.why_mvp: This is the one place on the whole table where the LLM is load-bearing rather than decorative: reading a beginner's stated belief in his own words and finding what is false in it against the engine's facts. It is the market skeptic's genuinely new idea moved to the one moment a player actually has something to say, with the piece still in his hand; it costs one quick call on an explicit tap and a few hours to build on top of K1's prompt builder and validator.
mvp_features.acceptance: 6...d6 position, Nxe5, click [data-action=but], type 'im attacking his king', press Enter, with window.__stubReplies = ['{"say":"You are, and the bishop on c4 already points at f7. But it is their move first, and the pawn on d6 takes the knight before you get there. Is there a square that still looks at their king that no pawn can reach?","squares":["d6","e5"]}']: __sampleCalls.slice(-1)[0].opts.modelTier === 'quick', opts.cache === false, opts.tools.length === 0, input contains 'im attacking his king'; within 1.5 s .coach text equals the stub say, cells d6 and e5 have class 'lit', [data-action=but] is gone, the input is gone, and #board.dataset.state is still 'held'. A stub reply with squares ['h8'] shows the template line 'The pawn on d6 takes the knight. Still want to?' and increments window.__coachRejects. window.__stubErrors = [{code: 'not_granted'}] before the send: no reply, [data-action=but] hidden for the rest of the view, the hold otherwise unchanged. At 400 px with the input focused, the board's bounding box is fully inside the viewport.

mvp_features.name: The close card and the next game's line
mvp_features.description: On game over the serif line gives the result in two or three words and the card appears under the board: 'Pieces given away: N (last game M). Holds: H, K taken back. Free pieces taken: F.' with each hold as a small static board (board.js in static mode, 120 px) captioned by category in piece words, and one button [Again]. The next game opens with one remembered line built from the stored categories by a template ('Two holds last game, both a pawn you did not see. Watch the pawns.'). Pieces given away counts play-anyways that lost material plus unheld losses detected by the per-move verdicts.
mvp_features.why_mvp: The number he comes back for is one he can feel going down, and the next game's opening line is the cheapest possible memory; both are templates on the hold log and cost nothing.
mvp_features.acceptance: A scripted game ending in checkmate (load the Scholar's position, play Qxf7#) shows .close with text matching /Pieces given away: \d+/ and a [data-action=again] button; clicking it loads the start position with data-state=idle. After a game with two holds taken back, reload: .coach on the new game contains 'last game' and localStorage 'holdon.v1.games' parses to an array whose last entry has holds.length === 2.

mvp_features.name: Test hooks, stub and copy guard
mvp_features.description: window.__app = {load(fen), play(san) -> Promise<'committed'|'held'|'illegal'>, tap(square), action(name), fen(), state(), waitEngine(), holds(), stats()}; window.__coachRejects; window.__stubErrors honoured by coach.js when the stub is present (the next call rejects with that code). scripts/scenarios/holdon.js exports the named scenarios above for scripts/app_check.js --script. A copy test greps every string literal in app/src and app/index.html for blunder, mistake, inaccuracy and '??' and fails the build on any hit.
mvp_features.why_mvp: The brief requires the coach to be testable through a stub and the page to render fully without sample; the copy guard is the only way the no-labels rule survives the temptation to add 'for clarity'.
mvp_features.acceptance: NODE_PATH=/opt/node22/lib/node_modules node scripts/app_check.js --dir app --script scripts/scenarios/holdon.js exits 0 with report.ok === true; the same with --no-stub exits 0; node scripts/copy_check.js exits 0 and exits 1 when a test fixture string containing 'blunder' is injected.

later_features: Iteration two, 'Sit in their chair': next to 'Show me', the brave option: the board turns (the piece layer's coordinate mapping, flip-ready from day one; a fade under reduced motion), 'You are Black now. What would you take?', he makes the capture with his own finger, the count drops, the board turns back. The skeptic's strongest novelty claim, held back only because the rotation on a 400 px phone must be tested in Sambudh's hands first.

Iteration two, 'Play it again from here' on the close card: the worst played-anyway or unheld moment, already stored with its FEN from the in-play verdicts (no scoring pass), resumes against the same opponent with the hold active and that category primed; 'Answered' means he kept the piece this time.

Iteration two, db + user behind store.js: the hold log, counts and remembered line per person at data/users/{self}/, surviving the move from laptop to phone; the memory line after five games ('Four of your last six holds were a pawn. Pawns are the ones you don't see.') written by one quick Claude call from the category counts, cached 24 h.

Iteration two, the fading hand: a per-game hold budget equal to the average of the last three games minus one, down toward zero; the first zero-hold game announced before it starts ('No holds today. A real game.') and what the hold would have caught shown only at the close; clean games chained as marks on the board edge; the amber ring drawn visibly smaller as the hold rate falls.

Iteration two, 'Send this one': the held position, its question and answer squares in the URL hash (versioned, length-capped, parsed with URLSearchParams and validated through chess.js, text rendered with textContent); a friend opens it in any browser with no Claude, sees the same held piece and the same question, taps, watches the ghost, and only then reads 'Play a game that holds your hand before you give a piece away.'
Iteration two, playing Black, with the gate from Black's side and the book extended to 1.d4 and 1.e4 replies.

Iteration three, the live whisper: when a stored habit's precondition appears in a later game (a pawn can reach a piece of his) and the engine confirms the move he is about to make would lose to it, the hold's question is prefixed 'This one again.' with nothing marked; a habit with zero instances in three games retires with 'You stopped doing that.'

Iteration three, 'Read my game': once per game from an explicit button with a Stop and progress driven from the tools' execute: default tier, tools show_position({ply}) restricted to this game's plies and check({ply, move}) returning the engine's cp and best reply, writing three sentences in the coach's voice; a 30-90 s wait placed where he is already looking at a result.

Later, the two-chair drill built from his own holds (punish, then prevent), a strength setting (Easier / Like me / Harder as Skill Level plus gift rate), PGN download through the downloads capability, and sound.

moments.trigger: K1: a real hold fires (the gate's verdict on the player's drop, an explicit viewer action). Never on the tutorial hold, never on a clean move, never on the opponent's move. Zero calls in a clean game; a typical beginner game makes two to six.
moments.prompt_strategy: One prompt string of about 1.4 KB in three blocks, built by coach.js from facts.js. Block 1, fixed and version-tagged (v1): 'You are a chess coach sitting beside a player rated under 1000. The page has just held one of their moves before it landed. Write ONE question, as the coach, that makes the player look at the thing they skipped. Rules: at most 18 words; begin with Hold on.; name pieces in plain words (pawn, knight), never notation; never name any of the answer squares; never say the move to play; no evaluation numbers; never use the words blunder, mistake, inaccuracy. Use only the facts below.' Block 2, the fact sheet: 'Position (FEN): ... Player is White. Move being held: knight from f3 to e5, taking a pawn. If it lands: the pawn on d6 takes the knight (the knight on c6 could also). Nothing of White's can take back on e5. Net: a knight for a pawn. Look skipped: from their chair, what can they take. Answer squares the player should tap: d6 (best), c6 (right but not the cheapest). Squares you may name: e5, f3, d6, c6. Moves you may name: none. This game so far: 1 hold, taken back (a capture of a defended piece). Last game's line: Watch the pawns.' Block 3, the contract: 'Reply with only JSON: {"question": string, "if_right": string (at most 20 words, confirm and name the exchange in piece words), "if_partial": string (at most 20 words, for a right-but-not-cheapest tap), "if_wrong": string (a hint, at most 14 words, naming no answer square)}'. Default cache (the history line makes repeats rare and a replay is harmless). A fresh AbortController per call, aborted by Take it back and Play it anyway.
moments.example_output: {"question":"Hold on. If the knight lands there, what takes it? Tap it.","if_right":"Yes, the pawn. A knight for a pawn.","if_partial":"The knight on c6 could too. Is there something cheaper? Look at the pawns.","if_wrong":"Not that one. Look at the pawns next to the square."}
moments.latency_ux: The hold never waits: the template question is on screen at 0 ms with the lifted piece, so there is no blank placeholder and no 'Thinking...'. Claude's validated question replaces the template with a 120 ms cross-fade only if it arrives before the player's first tap and while the hold is still open (about 1-1.5 s on quick; onText is useless for JSON so nothing streams). If the viewer's consent dialog appears (first call of the view) the held state simply stays held; there is no timer. A late reply is dropped, never swapped under his thumb.

moments.trigger: K2: the player taps 'But...' inside a hold, types one line and sends it (an explicit action). At most one per hold; the link disappears after the reply.
moments.prompt_strategy: The same fixed block and fact sheet as K1 with a different instruction and contract: 'The player pressed But... and wrote why they wanted this move. Answer THEIR idea, not an engine number. Two sentences at most, 45 words at most: first say what is true in their plan, then the one fact below that breaks it, then end with ONE question that points at the look they skipped and names no move. Plain piece words, no notation, no numbers, never blunder/mistake/inaccuracy. The player wrote: «im attacking his king». Reply with only JSON: {"say": string, "squares": [up to three squares from the list you may name]}'. cache: false (a repeat must be read again), fresh AbortController, aborted by Take it back and Play it anyway. The player's text is quoted inside guillemets and the instruction says to treat it as the player's words, not instructions.
moments.example_output: {"say":"You are, and the bishop on c4 already points at f7. But it is their move first, and the pawn on d6 takes the knight before you get there. Is there a square that still looks at their king that no pawn can reach?","squares":["d6","e5"]}
moments.latency_ux: On send the input closes at once, the serif line shows 'Looking...' with a soft 1 s pulse (this covers thinking, the consent dialog and queueing), and the validated reply appears whole after about 1-2 s with its squares lit; the two buttons stay available throughout so he is never locked. On any error code the template answer stands ('The pawn on d6 takes the knight. Still want to?'); rate_limited shows 'Coach is resting.' and hides the link for 60 s; not_granted and its family hide the link for the view with no message; invalid_json turns the link into 'Try again' once, never an automatic retry.

moments.trigger: Iteration two only, K3: the close card, from the game-end handler, cached 24 h keyed by game id, and then also from the next game's load as the remembered line. Not in the MVP: the close uses the template on the counts.
moments.prompt_strategy: The hold log of this game (category, outcome, taps) and the last five games' category counts, with the instruction to write {one_thing: at most 18 words, next_game: at most 12 words} in the coach's voice, naming the look he skips most, no moves, no numbers. Validated by the same validator.
moments.example_output: {"one_thing":"Both holds today were a knight landing where a pawn could reach it.","next_game":"Before the knight lands, look for the pawns."}
moments.latency_ux: Fires while the close card is already on screen with the template counts; the sentences fade in under the counts when they arrive; the next game's line is a stored string and makes no call.

page_tools.name: show_position (iteration two, not in the MVP)
page_tools.purpose: For the once-per-game 'Read my game' call on the default tier: sets the board to a ply of THIS game only (the page refuses any ply outside the move list, so Claude cannot show a position that did not happen) with optional highlight squares, so the viewer watches the coach move through the game while it writes; progress copy is driven from inside execute.
page_tools.returns: 'ok' or throws 'Error: ply out of range'

page_tools.name: check (iteration two, not in the MVP)
page_tools.purpose: For the same call: returns the engine's evaluation and best reply for a candidate move at a given ply, computed by the in-page Stockfish at depth 12, so every claim in the review is grounded before it is written; at most a handful of rounds, each a separate request.

llm_design.grounding_rule: Two gates, one before and one after, and no tools in the beat. Before: facts.js computes the fact sheet from chess.js and the Worker (the held move, what takes it and what takes back with piece names, the net loss in points, the look skipped, the answer squares with the best marked, the allowed squares, the listed moves, the category) and the prompt contains nothing else; Claude never sees a position without the facts, never evaluates a move, never decides whether to hold, and never types a FEN. After: validate.js rejects any reply in which a named square is outside the allowed set, a SAN-shaped token (regex \b([KQRBN]?[a-h]?[1-8]?x?[a-h][1-8](=[QRBN])?|O-O(-O)?)\b) appears outside the listed moves, a signed or decimal number appears, the words blunder, mistake, inaccuracy or '??' appear, the question contains an answer square, or a word cap is exceeded; a rejected reply is replaced by the template silently and window.__coachRejects is incremented so the stub tests can assert that a deliberately bad reply never reaches the board. Grading of every tap uses chess.js's own answer set; Claude's text is only ever words on the line and squares to light, and the squares are drawn only if they exist in the fact sheet. The MVP hands Claude no tools because every fact it needs is already in the prompt and each tool round would be another request inside a beat that must feel like a beat.
llm_design.without_claude: Identical game minus one link. When claude.use('sample') is null (any browser outside the viewer, local testing, a friend's copy), when the viewer declines (not_granted), or on any error: the gate fires exactly the same, the lifted piece and the amber square appear, the template question for the category shows ('Hold on. If the knight lands there, what takes it? Tap it.'), the tap is graded by chess.js with the template follow-ups built from piece names ('Yes, the pawn. A knight for a pawn.'), Show me plays the engine's refutation, Take it back and Play it anyway work, the close card shows the counts, and the next game opens with the templated remembered line. 'But...' is simply absent, and nothing on the page looks missing because no control is ever shown disabled and no message mentions Claude.

spec.engine_design: Stockfish 18 lite (app/vendor/stockfish-18-lite-single.js + .wasm, 7.3 MB, single-threaded) in one Web Worker created at load, warmed with uci/isready and 'setoption name MultiPV', behind engine.js: a serialized command queue with search ids, an info-line parser (depth, multipv, score cp or mate, pv), a search(fen, {depth, multipv, searchmoves}) promise that resolves with the per-line scores and pvs and the bestmove, and a stop() that marks the current id stale so its late bestmove is discarded, never played. chess.js 1.4.0 (app/vendor/chess.js) does everything instantaneous: legality, SAN and UCI, FEN, game over, moves({verbose:true}) for the dots and rings, and attackers() per square for the fact sheet. All evaluations are converted to the player's side (Stockfish reports from the side to move; mate N maps to +/-(10000-N)). The schedule per move pair, designed so the single thread is never mid-search when a drop needs a verdict: (1) IDLE, player to move: go depth 12 multipv 2 on the current FEN (id k) as the pre-search; this yields evalBefore, the best move (and whether it is a free capture or a mate in one for him). (2) On drop: stop (id k stale), chess.js applies the move on a scratch board and builds the post-move facts synchronously (under 1 ms), then go depth 10 on the post-move FEN (id k+1), about 0.3 s on desktop and under 1 s on a phone; evalAfter is negated to the player's side, the best reply and whether it is a capture, check or mate 1 come from the pv. (3) gate.js verdict (pure function). (4) Clean: commit; opponent search go depth 8 multipv 6 (id k+2), sampler as below, bestmove in about 0.3-0.6 s; then back to (1). Held: no search runs while the hold is open; Take it back reuses the cached pre-search result, so the next drop costs only step (2); Play it anyway runs go depth 12 (id k+2) for the opponent's true best reply. The opponent: candidates within 80 cp of the top line, weighted 50/25/12/8/5; the top move is forced when it is a capture gaining 200 cp or more or a mate (so a hung piece is punished every time); the 80 cp window itself means it never hangs its queen or walks into mate in one; between its 5th and 25th moves, on a one-in-eight schedule with jitter, the gift: among the multipv candidates within 400 cp of best, pick one after which a bot minor piece is attacked by the player and (undefended or attacked by a pawn) per chess.js, then confirm with go depth 10 on that position (id k+3, about 0.3 s) that the player's best move is that capture and gains 200 cp or more from the player's side; if no candidate passes, no gift this move; the gift rate steps down a notch after a game with zero pieces given away. The first two replies to 1.e4 come from data/book.json (20 lines) so the opening is instant while the WASM warms (2-4 s on a phone; a bot move that is genuinely waiting on warm-up shows 'Warming up the other side...' in the status line, and the player's own first move never waits). Resignation: the bot's evaluation at or below -900 from its side after three consecutive bot moves. Show me: the ghost line is the reply pv's first one or two plies (the capture and, when the exchange has one, the recapture), played by ghost.js from a scratch Chess; the '-N' is chess.js's material difference across those plies. Mate categories: 'score mate 1' in the reply search (allowed) or in the pre-search (missed). Every number the gate uses, every refutation Show me plays, every answer square the tap is graded against, and every fact in Claude's prompt comes from this pipeline; the engine never speaks to the player and Claude never evaluates a position. Budget: a clean move costs one pre-search (while he thinks) plus one depth-10 verdict plus one depth-8 opponent search, all under 1.5 s end to end in headless Chromium and under 2.5 s on a mid-range phone; a hold costs nothing extra; a gift costs one more depth-10 search on the bot's turn.

information_architecture.contents: The board on the verified Italian after 3...Nf6, White at the bottom; the serif line 'Your move. Most people take on f7 here. Go on.'; empty action bar; 44 px header with 'Hold On' in small sans at left and a theme dot at right.
information_architecture.primary_action: Make a move (tap a piece, tap a square).

information_architecture.contents: The board with the last move tinted; the line 'Your move.' (or, at the start of games two onward, the remembered line, e.g. 'Two holds last game, both a pawn you did not see. Watch the pawns.'); an empty action bar; occasionally a grey one-word chip 'Looked.' or the green ring and 'Free knight. You looked.'
The piece on its new square at full opacity, input locked, nothing drawn; a faint dot on the piece only if the verdict takes longer than 250 ms.

The piece lifted with a shadow over the destination, the destination breathing amber, other squares dimmed; the line 'Hold on. ...' with one question whose answer is a square; action bar [Take it back] [Play it anyway]; links 'Show me' and 'But...' under the line.
information_architecture.primary_action: Tap the square you think answers the question.

information_architecture.contents: The same board with the tapped square ringed green (right or partial) or the hint line (wrong; after a second wrong tap the answer square glows and is named); the same buttons and links.
information_architecture.primary_action: Take it back (primary) or Play it anyway.

information_architecture.contents: Real pieces at 35 percent, ghost pieces playing the capture at 50 percent, the serif '-N' floating from his board edge, a beat, then everything slides back to the hold.

A one-line input in the action bar with placeholder 'Say what you were going for' and a send button; the board scaled to stay visible above the keyboard; on send, 'Looking...' in the line, then the coach's two sentences with up to three squares lit; the input gone; the two buttons still present.
information_architecture.primary_action: Type one line and send; then Take it back or Play it anyway.

information_architecture.contents: The board with the player's move committed; the line unchanged; under 1 s with no indicator, or '...' after 800 ms, or 'Warming up the other side...' only when a bot move is truly waiting on engine warm-up.
The opponent's capture slides in; one sentence in the line ('There it goes. A knight for a pawn. You saw it coming; that counts.'); back to Your move.

The final position; the line 'Checkmate. Well played.' / 'That one got away.' / 'Black gives up. You are a queen ahead and it knows it.'; the close card under the board: 'Pieces given away: 1 (last game 4). Holds: 3, two taken back. Free pieces taken: 2.' with each hold as a small static board captioned in piece words; one button [Again].

information_architecture.screen_or_state: Coach unavailable (sample null, declined, or an error)
information_architecture.contents: Nothing visibly different: the same holds with template questions, the same buttons and Show me; the 'But...' link is absent; after rate_limited the line says 'Coach is resting.' for a minute.

visual_direction.mood: A tournament hall, not an app: a vinyl board on a quiet table, a coach beside you who speaks in a book's serif and otherwise says nothing. Calm, warm where the board is, cool everywhere else. The only movement on the page is pieces moving; the only colour that ever raises its voice is the amber of a held square. Relief, not shame: nothing on this page is ever red, there is no bar, no label, no score, no card grid. It should look like chess to a person who has never seen an AI product and like craft to a person who has.
visual_direction.palette: Tokens on :root, redefined under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) guarded by :root:not([data-theme=light]) and again under :root[data-theme=dark], with an explicit body background. Light: --bg #f3f4f1 (cool off-white), --ink #1f2430 (slate), --muted #6b7280, --coach #243b6b (ink blue, the serif line and the primary button), --hold #c98a1b (amber), --ok #4f7a4a (the green ring, used only for a right tap and a free piece taken), --square-light #e9e5d8 (pale sand), --square-dark #8f9a7e (sage), --tint rgba(36,59,107,.22) for the last move, --piece-white #f4f1e6 with outline #2a2a2a, --piece-black #2b2b2b with edge #f4f1e6. Dark: --bg #141821 (near-black blue-grey), --ink #e6e8ee, --muted #9aa3b2, --coach #9db4e8 (pale ink blue), --hold #e0a53a, --ok #7fae78, --square-light #b8b4a0, --square-dark #5c6b5a, the board remaining the warmest and brightest object on the page. The amber hold glow is a box-shadow inset, never a fill, so pieces stay legible on it.
visual_direction.type: The coach's line in Source Serif 4 (Google Fonts; fallback Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif) at 19 px / 1.35 on phone and 21 px on desktop, regular weight, sentence case, clamped to three lines with a fixed height so the board never jumps. Labels, buttons, counts and the header in IBM Plex Sans (fallback system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif) at 14 px, medium weight, sentence case, no uppercase tracking. The '-N' float and the coordinates in the serif at 13 px. Never Inter, never a display font, never bold serif headlines; the page has no headline at all.
