visual_direction.board: A static 64-cell CSS grid, square, width min(100vw - 32px, 62vh) (46 px squares at 400 px), 1 px --muted border at 20 percent, 4 px radius, coordinates as 10 px letters inside the a-file and first-rank squares in the opposite square tint. Pieces: twelve hand-drawn flat silhouettes (chunky, legible at 46 px, no gradients, no faces) as inline SVG symbols, white pieces ivory with a 1.5 px ink outline, black pieces charcoal with a 1 px ivory edge, each piece a focusable button on an absolutely positioned layer moved by transform. Overlays, back to front: last-move tint; legal dots (10 px, ink at 35 percent) and capture rings (2 px ring); the hold dim (a 12 percent ink overlay on every square but the destination); the amber inset glow on the destination; the green ring; the lit squares from a Claude reply (a 2 px --coach ring); one SVG layer for the single arrow drawn after a second wrong tap; the ghost piece layer at 50 percent opacity above the real layer, which drops to 35 percent during Show me. The held piece: translateY(-6px) scale(1.06) with a 0 8px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.28) shadow, full opacity, so it is visibly off the square, not dimmed on it. Below the board: a 56 px action bar that is empty until a decision is needed, with one ink primary button and one quiet secondary; the two text links sit at the end of the coach line, not in the bar. Above the board: the 44 px header ('Hold On' small, left; a theme dot, right). No move list, no eval bar, no clock, no rating, no settings gear on the first frame.
visual_direction.motion: Pieces slide 150 ms ease-out by transform; a picked-up piece scales to 1.06 with a shadow in 100 ms; the amber hold breathes on a 1.6 s inset-glow loop; the coach line cross-fades 120 ms when Claude's question replaces the template; Show me plays 600 ms per ply, the '-N' rises 18 px and fades over 700 ms, a 500 ms beat, then a 300 ms rewind; the take-back slide is the same 150 ms as a move; the green ring holds 900 ms; the 'Looked.' chip fades after 1.2 s. Under prefers-reduced-motion every duration is 0, the breathe becomes a static amber ring, the float becomes a static '-N' label beside the board for 1.2 s, and Show me shows the final ghost position statically. Nothing bounces, nothing slides in from off-screen, no confetti.
visual_direction.what_to_avoid: An eval bar, a move list, a rating, a clock, a '??' or 'Blunder' label, anything red, a speech bubble or chat balloon, a chat box, a settings gear or strength slider on the first frame, a dashboard of stats, rounded cards everywhere, the cream-and-terracotta or acid-green-on-black or purple-gradient AI defaults, Inter, emoji anywhere, uppercase tracked labels, Unicode chess glyphs as pieces, a hollow 'empty state' screen, a tutorial overlay with arrows and tooltips, and any copy that addresses the player as a user ('Submit', 'Analyze', 'Accuracy').

spec.persistence: store.js exposes {get, set, append, list} and in the MVP is backed by localStorage only, every read and write wrapped in try/catch so a private window or blocked storage still plays: holdon.v1.tutorialSeen ('1'), holdon.v1.theme ('light' | 'dark' | unset, set by the header dot and written to data-theme on :root), holdon.v1.games (the last five game summaries: {id, date, result, givenAway, holds: [{fen, san, category, taps, outcome}], freeTaken, playedAnyway}), holdon.v1.holds (the last thirty hold moments across games, the material for the remembered line and, in iteration two, for 'Play it again from here' and 'Send this one'). Nothing about the current game is persisted mid-game in the MVP (a reload starts a new game). Iteration two moves games and holds to the db + user capabilities at data/users/{self}/games and data/users/{self}/holds behind the same store.js interface, with localStorage kept as a mirror and for conveniences only, because localStorage is per browser and Sambudh will switch from laptop to phone; the builder reads the artifact-capabilities skill for db's exact API before writing that path, noting that viewers of a public link who are not the owner never write.
success_criteria: In headless Chromium (scripts/app_check.js with scripts/scenarios/holdon.js): every acceptance scenario above passes, report.ok is true at 1280 px and 400 px in light and dark, with zero console errors, zero page errors, zero failed requests and no horizontal overflow; the same run with --no-stub passes with [data-action=but] absent.

The gate is right on every verified position: it holds on Nxe5, Bxf7+ (both Italian positions), O-O in the Ruy, Nc3 after 4...Nxe4, Nbd2 in the placement position, O-O after 5...Ng4, g4 after 1.f3 e5 and Qh3 in the Scholar's position, and stays silent on h3, d3, Ba4, dxe4, hxg4 (both positions) and Qxf7#; a clean six-move sequence makes zero sample calls.

The beat holds: from drop to verdict under 1.5 s in headless Chromium and under 2.5 s on a mid-range phone; the template question is on screen at 0 ms of the hold; the opponent replies within 1 s on non-gift moves; the page's own first move never waits on engine warm-up.

Claude is never wrong on the board: every stub reply that names an off-list square, a SAN token outside the listed moves, a number, a banned word, or an answer square inside the question is rejected (window.__coachRejects increments) and the template shows; no square is ever lit that is not in the fact sheet.

Sambudh, in his first session: understands the first screen without a word of instruction, reaches the real game within 45 s having pressed both Take it back and Play it anyway at least once, finishes a game (the bot resigns or mates), takes back at least one hold per game, takes at least one free piece per game, and his second game ends with fewer pieces given away than his first.
The mission's own measure, over the first week: three of five games with zero pieces given away, read off the close card's count, with the hold firing less often from game to game.
Scope discipline holds: the shipped page contains no eval bar, move list, rating, clock, chat box, red colour, '??' or the words blunder, mistake or inaccuracy (the copy test enforces the last four).

Cost: a typical game spends at most six quick-tier calls plus the But... calls the player chose to make, each under 2 KB, none with tools, none from a timer or loop, and the consent dialog only ever appears over a stable held state.
risks: Over-holding turns the coach into a nag: the thresholds (200 cp AND a capture or mate refutation AND a chess.js-nameable mechanism) must be enforced by the scenario tests, never by taste, and the quiet-after-two-play-anyways and never-the-same-square rules must ship on day one.

The opponent is the hardest engineering and is untested on real beginners: a sampler inside 80 cp may still play engine-shaped moves, the gift may rarely qualify in closed positions, and a bot that gives nothing teaches only defence; tune with a few hundred headless self-play games before Sambudh sees it, and keep the gift rate and window as two constants.

Engine warm-up on a slow phone is 2-4 s and a depth-10 verdict can approach a second: the pending state must be honest (the dot after 250 ms), the book must cover the first replies, and the verdict budget must be measured on a real Android, not only in headless Chromium.

The consent dialog appears over the first real hold (K1) or the first But... (K2); the held state is stable so nothing is lost, but a confused viewer may decline and never see the feature; the tutorial before any call is the mitigation, and the copy must never make the game look broken when Claude is absent.

The quick tier may ignore the rules (name the answer square, add a number, write three sentences): the validator and the template fallback make this invisible, but a high rejection rate would mean Claude never speaks; measure window.__coachRejects on real calls and tighten the prompt rather than loosen the validator.

Typing in But... on a phone: the keyboard covers the board unless the board scales with visualViewport, and a long reply pushes the line to three lines; if real use shows it is rarely pressed, it stays a link and costs nothing, but it must never become a standing text box.
Drawing twelve piece silhouettes that are legible at 46 px is a real afternoon; if it slips, ship chunkier simpler shapes rather than a third-party set with a licence question beside the GPL engine.

localStorage is per browser: the close card's 'last game' and the remembered line vanish when he moves from laptop to phone; db + user must follow in iteration two before the memory story is promised in copy.

Scope creep toward Lichess: an eval bar, a move list, a strength slider and a rating are each one argument away and each turns this back into the commodity; the copy test and the information architecture above are the defence.
Licensing: shipping Stockfish (GPLv3) inside the page means the page's own source should be published under a GPL-compatible licence; flagged in app/LICENSE.md, not solved, in the MVP.
open_questions: Should the gate stay active when the player is already five or more points down (the coach's suppression rule, which the beginner rejected: 'when I'm losing badly is exactly when I want the hand on my wrist')? The MVP keeps it active and relies on the play-anyway rules; Sambudh's first bad game decides.

Is the tutorial's dare ('Most people take on f7 here. Go on.') welcome or patronising on a second viewing by someone who already plays? It appears once per browser; if it grates, the fallback is the designer's plainer 'Your move. The first three moves are the usual ones.'

Gift rate and sampler window (one in eight, 80 cp) are guesses at an 800-strength opponent; what do a hundred headless self-play games and Sambudh's first three games say about how often he gets to take something and how often he loses anyway?

Which look does he actually skip most, and does the hold's question need to rotate across categories to stay a question rather than a reflex? The hold log answers this after five games and decides whether K1's history line earns its place.

Does 'But...' get pressed at all on a phone, and when it is, does Claude's reply beat the template in a blind comparison on the same twenty holds? If not, the link stays but the LLM leaves it; if yes, it becomes the headline of the share link in iteration two.

Chair swap versus ghost for 'Show me' in iteration two: the market skeptic's strongest novelty claim is taking your own piece with your own finger; it needs the flip tested in Sambudh's hands on a 400 px phone before it is the default.
Which licence for the page's own source, given the GPLv3 engine inside it; and does the piece set we draw get released with it?

refuted.claim: Engine latency: 'go depth 10 on the new position, about 0.3 s', 'each verdict arrives within 1.5 s of the drop', opponent search 'bestmove in about 0.3-0.6 s', 'depth 12 multipv 2 while he thinks' needing a stop-and-discard dance.
refuted.why_wrong: The vendored WASM at the spec's exact depths is 10-50x faster than budgeted. The pending dot (>250 ms), the '...' (>800 ms) and the 'late bestmove discarded by search id' machinery are designed around a latency that does not exist in headless Chromium, and a 50 ms stop already has a depth-10 pre-search in hand, so the evalBefore-from-a-stopped-search worry is moot on desktop. The real latency item is the 7.3 MB download plus compile on a phone (brief: 2-4 s), which the spec never gives a cold-engine policy for.
refuted.evidence: Probe at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-hello-world/272d20b6-49d9-50c7-82a4-431be1d3a0e1/scratchpad/probe.js (output probe-out.json), real worker from app/vendor in headless Chromium: warm-up uci→readyok 368 ms; verdict go depth 10 on the eight spec positions 1-42 ms; pre-search depth 12 multipv 2 11-243 ms; opponent depth 8 multipv 6 3-77 ms; 'stop' sent 50 ms into the pre-search returned depth 10 in 92 ms. All 13 position/move pairs plus the stop test ran in 1.9 s total.

refuted.claim: K1/K2 validator: 'no SAN-shaped token outside the listed moves' with regex \b([KQRBN]?[a-h]?[1-8]?x?[a-h][1-8](=[QRBN])?|O-O(-O)?)\b, plus 'no signed number', while the K2 acceptance expects the example reply 'the pawn on d6 takes the knight...' to be ACCEPTED and shown.
refuted.why_wrong: The regex's [a-h][1-8] core matches every bare square name, so with 'Moves you may name: none' the validator rejects the spec's own example outputs and Claude never speaks (window.__coachRejects goes to 100%). The number check has the same trap: a naive [-+]?\d+ sees the '6' in 'd6'. The validator must be a pipeline: extract squares, check subset of allowed, mask them, then SAN (requiring a piece letter, 'x', '=' or O-O), then numbers, then banned words, then caps.
refuted.evidence: node -e run of the spec's regex against the spec's K2 example_output returned ['c4','f7','d6'] and against the K1 if_partial example returned ['c6']; the K2 acceptance says 'within 1.5 s .coach text equals the stub say'.

refuted.claim: Gate 'Categories in priority: allowed_mate; hanging_after_move (...); ignored_attack (the same, but chess.js says that piece was already attacked before his move)' together with the acceptance 'Ruy after 3...a6: O-O held with hold=ignored_attack'.
refuted.why_wrong: Under the stated priority order hanging_after_move's conditions are all satisfied for O-O (cpLoss 411, best reply axb5 is a capture, bishop b5 attacked-and-undefended, net loss 3) so it fires first and the test can never see ignored_attack. The two categories need a discriminator the spec never states: hanging_after_move = the captured piece is the moved piece (or newly attacked by the move); ignored_attack = a different piece that was attacked before the move. The 'he moved the defender away' case, the commonest under-1000 mechanism, falls in neither template's wording ('If the knight lands there, what takes it?' is wrong when the knight is not what gets taken).
refuted.evidence: Probe P3: evalBefore 37, after O-O evalAfter -374, cpLoss 411, reply a6b5 capture; spec gate text and acceptance for 'The silent gate'.

refuted.claim: Tutorial: 'The gate runs as normal but the question and follow-ups for this position are canned' and the first_30_seconds timeline that puts the Bxf7+ hold at 3-8 s on a phone where 'the 7 MB engine is warming... he never waits on it'.
refuted.why_wrong: If the gate runs as normal the tutorial hold needs a warm engine; first_30_seconds itself says 'This hold is canned (the position is verified, the answer set is {e8})'. The two sentences contradict, and the brief's own number (2-4 s warm-up on a phone, before counting a 7.3 MB download on cellular) makes the engine path lose the race on exactly the first screen the whole design depends on. The same gap exists for the real game's first two moves: the book covers the bot, nothing covers the verdict on 1.e4 while the WASM is cold.
refuted.evidence: BRIEF.md platform section ('7.3 MB'); spec engine_design ('2-4 s on a phone'); probe warm-up 368 ms even on the build machine; spec 'The tutorial hold' description vs first_30_seconds step 3-8 s.

refuted.claim: Test hooks: 'scripts/scenarios/holdon.js exports the named scenarios above for scripts/app_check.js --script'; 'the stub reports the K1 call as cancelled if it had not resolved'; 'window.__stubErrors honoured by coach.js when the stub is present'.
refuted.why_wrong: The existing harness loads ONE exported async (page, ctx) function and runs it four times (desktop/phone x light/dark, each a fresh page and a fresh WASM warm-up); its stub records only {input, opts:{modelTier, tools names, cache}} per call, never an outcome, and has no error-injection hook. 'Reported as cancelled' is unobservable from window.__sampleCalls, and 'honoured by coach.js' puts a test variable into production code. Either extend STUB_SCRIPT (record outcome per call, read __stubErrors) or drop those three assertions.
refuted.evidence: /home/user/hello-world/scripts/app_check.js: STUB_SCRIPT calls.push({ input, opts: {...} }) with no result field; 'const fn = require(path.resolve(SCENARIO)); await fn(page, { vp, scheme, report })' inside the 2x2 viewport/scheme loop.

refuted.claim: Opponent acceptance: 'From the verified position after 4.d3 Nxe4 loaded with the bot to move: the bot's reply is dxe4 10 times out of 10'.
refuted.why_wrong: That position is White to move; making the bot play it means a bot-as-White / player-as-Black path, which later_features lists as 'Iteration two, playing Black'. The forced-capture rule itself is fine (and the test's chess holds), but the test demands a mode the MVP excludes. Use a Black-to-move position instead, e.g. P1 after Nxe5 where the bot must reply dxe5 (already the Play-it-anyway acceptance) or P3 after O-O where it must reply axb5.
refuted.evidence: Probe botP4 (White to move, depth 8 multipv 6): d3e4 386 vs c4f7 71; probe P1 after Nxe5 bot lines d6e5 382, c6e5 342; spec later_features item 6.

refuted.claim: Rewards: 'When their last move newly attacked a piece of his and after his move nothing of his is hanging: ... Looked.' tested by 'Ruy after 3...a6: play("Ba4") -> a .chip'.
refuted.why_wrong: window.__app.load(fen) carries no last move, so 'their last move newly attacked' is undefined in every acceptance scenario; the rule must be restated in FEN-derivable terms (a non-pawn piece of his attacked-and-undefended or by a cheaper piece before his move, nothing hanging after) or the chip fires on most opening moves (e4 attacked by Nf6 after 3...Nf6 would make 4.d3 'Looked.') or never.
refuted.evidence: Spec 'Rewards for the look' description vs acceptance; test hooks list load(fen) only.

refuted.claim: Copy guard: 'greps every string literal in app/src and app/index.html for blunder, mistake, inaccuracy and ?? and fails the build on any hit'.
refuted.why_wrong: validate.js in app/src must hold exactly those words as its ban list ('none of blunder/mistake/inaccuracy/??'), so the guard as specified fails the build on the validator it protects. Exclude validate.js (or build the list from a regex / char codes) and the stub fixtures that deliberately contain 'blunder'.
refuted.evidence: Spec 'Claude K1' description (validate.js rejects 'none of blunder/mistake/inaccuracy/??') and 'Test hooks, stub and copy guard' description; acceptance 'A reply containing blunder is rejected'.

must_change: Rewrite validate.js as an ordered pipeline and fix the regex: (1) extract every [a-h][1-8] token, require it to be in the allowed set (and, for K1's question, not in the answer set), then mask those tokens; (2) SAN check on the masked text with a regex that requires a piece letter, an 'x', a '=' or O-O (the spec's regex matches bare squares and rejects its own example outputs; verified by running it); (3) number check on the masked text; (4) banned words; (5) word caps. Add a unit test that the spec's two example_output JSONs pass.

Define the gate categories so the acceptance is reachable: hanging_after_move only when the piece the best reply captures is the piece he just moved (or became attackable because of the move); ignored_attack when it is a different piece that chess.js already saw attacked before the move; add the 'moved the defender' case to ignored_attack with its own template ('Hold on. Something of yours just lost its guard. Tap it.'). Under the spec's stated priority, the Ruy O-O test (cpLoss 411, reply axb5) fires hanging_after_move, never ignored_attack.

Make the tutorial hold engine-independent: detect Bxf7+ / Nxe5 by SAN match on the known FEN with canned answer sets, no verdict search; and state the cold-engine policy for real moves (while the Worker is not ready, the player's move commits silently with no verdict and the bot uses the book or 'Warming up the other side...'). The spec contradicts itself ('the gate runs as normal' vs 'This hold is canned') and the phone's 2-4 s warm-up plus a 7.3 MB download lands exactly on the 3-8 s first hold.

Reconcile the test plan with /home/user/hello-world/scripts/app_check.js: export one async (page, ctx) function that runs the scenarios in sequence (it runs four times, fresh page each time); add to the harness STUB_SCRIPT an outcome field per recorded call (resolved / cancelled / error code) and an error-injection hook (window.__stubErrors consumed by the stub, not by coach.js); drop 'the stub reports the K1 call as cancelled' unless that is done; replace the bot-as-White dxe4 test with a Black-to-move position (after Nxe5 in the 6...d6 position: dxe5 10/10), since playing Black is iteration two; add a window.__app.fast flag that zeroes animation durations so 45 assertions x 4 runs stay under ~3 minutes.

Restate the 'Looked.' chip rule in FEN-derivable terms (a non-pawn piece of his attacked-and-undefended or by a cheaper piece before the move, nothing hanging after) because load(fen) has no 'their last move'; keep the 6...d6 h3 negative test to prove it stays quiet.
Fix the copy guard so it does not fail on validate.js's own ban list or on stub fixtures: exclude app/src/validate.js (or assemble the words from a regex/char codes) and scripts/scenarios/*.

Cut the one-session scope explicitly and in this order of what ships: tap-tap only (drag is the enhancement, keep its code path out of v1), auto-queen promotion (strip later), opening book of 6-8 lines, close card with text captions instead of mini static boards, the gift rule behind a GIFT_RATE constant that defaults to 0 until a 20-game headless smoke exists (there is no time in-session for 'a few hundred self-play games'), and a piece set decision made before coding: the repo has nothing to reuse (/home/user/hello-world/chess-study/components/local/board.js renders Unicode GLYPHs), so commit to twelve chunky geometric silhouettes (circle/trapezoid/cross builds, no 'hand-drawn' ambition) with a fixed two-hour cap.
nice_to_change: Re-base the latency budget on measured numbers (verdict 1-42 ms, pre-search 11-243 ms, bot 3-77 ms, warm-up 368 ms in headless Chromium): raise the verdict to depth 12 and the pre-search to depth 14 for free, keep the pending dot and '...' as code paths but accept they are untestable without an injected delay, and add a minimum ~400 ms before the bot's reply slides so the opponent's move reads as a move rather than a flicker.

Determinism of scenario runs: fixed-depth evals drift 15-25 cp between runs because the pre-search is stopped at a time-dependent point and the transposition table carries over (P5 Nbd2 cpLoss 312 vs 289, P6 O-O 304 vs 288, P4 evalBefore 411 vs 393 across two probe runs). All eight test positions have at least 70 cp of margin over the 200 threshold (closest: tutorial Nxe5 at 271, Bxf7+ at 278), but send 'ucinewgame' before each verdict search, or set Hash to 1 MB, so the gate tests cannot flake.

Pick one forced-capture rule for the opponent: core_loop says 'captures two points or more', the feature says 'a capture gaining 200 cp or more' with no reference point. Suggest: top candidate is a capture AND (chess.js net gain >= 2 points OR it leads the second line by >= 150 cp). Both the Nxe5 (dxe5 382 vs Nxe5 342, both captures) and Nxe4 (dxe4 386 vs Bxf7+ 71) cases pass either way, but the rule must be one sentence in code.

Guard the two things that flip report.ok in the harness: ship an inline favicon (<link rel="icon" href="data:,">; a bare page in the probe logged a 404 console error on cold load) and never call console.error from page code, since every real hold in a scenario without a canned reply makes the stub's sample.json reject invalid_json by design.

Resolve sample lazily: the contract says claude.use('sample') may settle null only ~10 s after load when framed by a non-Claude host, so decide the But... link's presence when the promise settles and on the first error code, not once at load.

Accept and state the K1 cost model honestly: a quick call is paid on every real hold and dropped whenever he taps inside ~1.5 s; cap the cross-fade window (swap only within ~2.5 s of the hold) so the question never changes under a reader mid-sentence, and record dropped-vs-shown in the hold log so the first week says whether K1 earns its call.

Note that the 400 px 'board inside the viewport with the input focused' assertion is vacuous in headless Chromium (no OS keyboard); keep it, but mark visualViewport scaling as phone-only verification.

Add 'ucinewgame' + 'isready' at game start and a serialized queue rule that a new 'go' waits for the previous 'bestmove' after 'stop' (the UCI engine ignores a 'go' sent mid-search); the probe's queue did this and never desynced.
critiques.strongest_part: The silent gate and the engine pipeline are real, not aspirational: running the actual vendored Stockfish 18 lite WASM worker in headless Chromium at the spec's exact depths, all thirteen (position, move) pairs the acceptance names produce the verdict the spec predicts (Nxe5 423, Bxf7+ 391, h3 42 in the 6...d6 position; tutorial Bxf7+ 278, Nxe5 271, d3 8; Ruy O-O 411 with reply axb5, Ba4 1; Nc3 542 with pre-search best dxe4 of a pawn-attacked knight, dxe4 -6; Nbd2 289 and O-O 288 with the pre-search best being the free capture; g4 answered by Qh4 mate 1; Qh3 after a pre-search mate 1), every 'clean' move under 50 cp, every best reply a capture exactly where the category needs one, and the whole batch in 1.9 s with a 368 ms warm-up. The pure-function gate over chess.js attackers() (which does report defenders, verified in the vendored source) plus a fully template-driven no-Claude path means the product is playable, testable and honest before a single sample call exists, which is the right order for a one-session build.

critiques.lens: Beginner value: would Sambudh (under 1000, studied nothing, loses to hanging pieces and one-move threats, phone in one hand, 10-15 minutes) actually get stronger and come back tomorrow? Evidence: /home/user/hello-world/product/BRIEF.md, /home/user/hello-world/.claude/agents/chess-master.md (the under-1000 band: the three looks before every move, piece values, basic mates), /home/user/hello-world/chess-study/lessons/0001-blunder-check.yml and 0000-placement.yml (the verified positions the spec cites), and two Stockfish runs I made with the tintins binary: every White move in the tutorial position judged at depth 14, and a six-game self-play of the spec's exact opponent recipe (depth 8, multipv 6, 80 cp window, 50/25/12/8/5, forced capture, gift rule with depth-10 verification) against Stockfish limited to UCI_Elo 1320, script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-hello-world/272d20b6-49d9-50c7-82a4-431be1d3a0e1/scratchpad/holdon_bot_sim.py.

refuted.claim: The opponent 'plays like an 800 (it leaves pieces for you and always takes yours)' (thesis; core_loop 9; engine_design).
refuted.why_wrong: An 800 does not beat a 1300 six times out of six. The recipe as written (candidates within 80 cp of the depth-8 best, weighted toward the top) is an engine with a little noise; it is far above Sambudh, so he loses on position in every game in which he gives nothing away, and the close card's 'Pieces given away: 0' will sit next to a loss. 'Always takes yours' does work (the bot took 25 free pieces in six games), which makes it a punisher without being a peer.
refuted.evidence: Self-play, six games, the spec's recipe vs Stockfish 18 with UCI_LimitStrength true and UCI_Elo 1320 (the engine's floor: 'option name UCI_Elo ... min 1320'): bot score 6.0/6, games of 47-70 plies, every one ended by checkmate of the 1320 side. Script and output: holdon_bot_sim.py in the scratchpad (seed 7; the forced-capture rule read as top move is a capture and leads the runner-up by 200 cp or more; six games is a small sample but 6-0 with the opponent never once winning is not a sampling accident).

refuted.claim: The gift rule gives him a free piece 'roughly one move in eight' between the bot's 5th and 25th moves, 'so he gets to be the one who looks and takes' (core_loop 9; engine_design: 'among the multipv candidates within 400 cp of best, pick one after which a bot minor piece is attacked ... confirm with go depth 10').
refuted.why_wrong: The six multipv lines at depth 8 are by definition the six best moves; a move that drops a minor piece is about -300, so it is in that list only when fewer than six moves are better than -300, which in a middlegame almost never happens. The one-in-eight schedule therefore multiplies a near-zero. The reward 'Free knight. You looked.' and the resignation line are unreachable, and the free-capture look (half of what loses games at this level, per the spec's own why_mvp) gets no reps.
refuted.evidence: Same six games: of 116 bot moves inside the 5-25 window, a qualifying candidate existed in 3 (2.6 percent); with the 1/8 roll, gifts given = 0 in six games. The 1320-rated Stockfish, by contrast, hung a piece 44 times in the same games, which is what an opponent at Sambudh's level actually looks like.

refuted.claim: 'It resigns when nine or more points down for three of its own moves, so games end: Black gives up. You are a queen ahead and it knows it.' (core_loop 9) and the success criterion 'finishes a game (the bot resigns or mates)'.
refuted.why_wrong: Even if the gift rule worked at its stated rate, 20 windows / 8 is about 2.5 minor pieces, 7.5 points, under the 9-point threshold; and the bot 'always takes yours', so every piece he gives back pushes the number up again. Against a defence that goes 6-0 versus a 1320, a sub-1000 player will not win nine points by tactics the bot did not intend. In practice the only game-ending event in the spec is the bot mating him, so 'That one got away.' is the ending he sees, every time, in his 10-15 minutes.
refuted.evidence: Arithmetic on core_loop 9's own numbers (one in eight over moves 5-25, minor pieces only, resign at -900 x 3); the self-play above: 0 gifts in 6 games and the bot never below +3 at adjudication.

refuted.claim: In the tutorial, 'if he played a safe move like 4.d3 the line says Safe. Now try the one everyone plays' and 'the answer sets are {e8} for Bxf7+ and {c6} for Nxe5' (first_30_seconds; mvp_features: The tutorial hold).
refuted.why_wrong: The canned table has two held moves and treats every other move as safe. A beginner who plays the beginner's attacking move 4.Nd4?? (exd4), 4.Ba6?? (bxa6) or 4.Be6?? (dxe6) hangs a piece and is told 'Safe.' in the product's first thirty seconds, which is the one moment it has to prove it knows what it is talking about. The description also says 'the gate runs as normal', which needs the depth-10 verdict from a Worker the spec itself says takes 2-4 s to warm on a phone, while the hold is scheduled at 3-8 s.
refuted.evidence: My depth-14 run over all 32 legal White moves in r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/2B1P3/5N2/PPPP1PPP/RNBQK2R w KQkq - 4 4: loss >= 200 cp for Be6 (547), Nd4 (520), Ba6 (458), Bxf7+ (354), Nxe5 (306), Nh4 (265), Ng1, Ke2, Rf1, Kf1, Rg1, g4; the first three are pieces taken for free by a one-move capture, i.e. exactly what the gate holds in a real game. (Bd5 is only 81: Nxd5 exd5 is an even trade, so it is correctly 'safe'.) Warm-up: engine_design, 'the WASM warms (2-4 s on a phone)'.

refuted.claim: Tap-to-answer: 'hanging/ignored: the enemy squares that can capture the piece' (mvp_features: Tap-to-answer), and the priority list 'hanging_after_move' before 'ignored_attack' (core_loop 4; The silent gate).
refuted.why_wrong: The acceptance for the same feature says 'In the Ruy after 3...a6, O-O then tap(b5) is right' and the gate acceptance says O-O yields hold=ignored_attack. b5 is White's own bishop, not an enemy square, and O-O also satisfies hanging_after_move (attacked and undefended after the move), which the listed priority would pick first. A builder following the text builds one thing and the tests expect another; and which one ships changes what the beginner learns (the chess-master's first look is 'what did their last move attack', which is the b5 answer).
refuted.evidence: Spec text: Tap-to-answer description vs its acceptance; core_loop 4 priority (a)(b)(c) vs 'The silent gate' acceptance 'O-O held with hold=ignored_attack'; chess-master.md: 'the check before every move (what did their last move attack, what can they take, what checks do they have)'.

refuted.claim: K1 earns its place because 'only an LLM can choose which look to point at and phrase it for this position and this player's history' and 'templated questions become wallpaper by game five' (Claude K1 why_mvp).
refuted.why_wrong: The prompt never asks Claude to choose a look, only to write one question from a fact sheet in which the look is already chosen ('Look skipped: from their chair, what can they take'), and the spec's own example output is byte-for-byte the template question from core_loop 4(b). In the MVP as written, Sambudh never sees the LLM do anything the template does not; the one load-bearing LLM moment ('But...') is behind a link the spec admits he may never press.
refuted.evidence: llm_design.moments[0].example_output question = 'Hold on. If the knight lands there, what takes it? Tap it.' which equals core_loop 4(b)'s template verbatim; open_questions: 'Does But... get pressed at all on a phone'.

refuted.claim: The gate scenarios run 'from positions already verified at depth 20 in this repo' (thesis; The silent gate acceptance).
refuted.why_wrong: Two of the nine positions are not verified anywhere in the repo: the Fool's-mate FEN after 1.f3 e5 appears in no lesson, and the Scholar's White-to-move FEN is only derived from a Black-to-move verification. Low stakes (I confirmed 2.g4 is mate in one for Black myself), but the spec should not claim repo verification it does not have; add the two FENs to a verified fixture with engine_check.py comments.
refuted.evidence: grep of chess-study/lessons/*.yml: the 0001 lesson verifies the 4...Nxe4, 5...Ng4, Ruy 3...a6, Scholar's (b to move), Italian 3...Nf6 and 6...d6 positions; 0000 verifies the 7...O-O placement; neither contains rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/8/5P2/PPPPP1PP/RNBQKBNR or r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p2Q/2B1P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB1K1NR. My check: after 1.f3 e5 2.g4 Stockfish reports #-1.

must_change: The opponent must be calibrated by measurement, not by adjectives, and the gift mechanism must be rebuilt so it actually fires. Replace 'plays like an 800' with an acceptance test: over 100 headless self-play games against Stockfish with UCI_LimitStrength true and UCI_Elo 1320 at depth 8, the Hold On bot scores at most 40 percent and leaves at least two depth-10-verified free minor pieces per game on average (the current recipe scores 100 percent and leaves zero). Concretely: (1) generate gift candidates by enumerating the bot's legal moves with chess.js and keeping those after which a bot minor piece is attacked by the player and undefended or attacked by a pawn, then verify one with a depth-10 search, instead of looking inside the six best lines where such moves never are; (2) allow gifts across the whole game, not only bot moves 5-25, and allow a gift to be a recapture or a careless capture, which is how an 800 actually loses pieces; (3) widen the sampler (80 cp to about 250 cp, or Skill Level 0-3 for non-forced moves) and re-measure; (4) keep 'always takes yours' exactly as written, it is the one part that works. Keep the gift rate and window as two constants and ship the self-play script with the repo.

Give him a way out of a lost game. The spec has no control between the first move and the close card (information_architecture lists none; persistence says 'a reload starts a new game'), the bot resigns only when it is losing, and the self-play shows he will be the one losing. Add a quiet text link 'Give up' (ink, never red, next to the theme dot or at the end of the coach line) with a one-tap confirm inside the serif line ('Give up this one? [Yes] [Keep playing]'), reaching the same close card with result 'You gave up' and all the holds counted; and a mirror of the bot's mercy: when he has been nine or more points down for three moves, the line offers 'Start again?' once. Without this his 10-15 minutes end in a position he cannot leave, and the close card, the count and the remembered line, the product's entire reason to come back, never appear.

The gate must never go silent on the two things that end his games. 'After the second play-anyway in a game the coach stays quiet until the close' and 'that piece-and-square pair is never held again this game' (core_loop 8) must not apply to allowed_mate, missed_mate, or any hold whose net loss is five points or more (a rook or the queen). Two curious play-anyways in the opening, which the tutorial literally invites, would otherwise switch the hand off for the move 20 queen blunder that is why he is here; the beginner's own words in open_questions ('when I'm losing badly is exactly when I want the hand on my wrist') already argue this. Add acceptance: after two play-anyways, g4 after 1.f3 e5 still holds and a move hanging the queen still holds.

The tutorial must not depend on the engine and its canned table must be complete. Store a verified verdict table for the 3...Nf6 position in data/tutorial.json (built with scripts/engine_check.py, comments beside each entry like the lessons do) that classifies every legal move: held with answer squares for Bxf7+ {e8}, Nxe5 {c6}, Nd4 {e5}, Ba6 {b7}, Be6 {d7, f7}; everything else accepted. The 'gate runs as normal' sentence goes; the Worker warms in the background and the first real game's first Black reply comes from the book, so nothing in the first 45 seconds waits on WASM (the spec promises 'he never waits on it' and then schedules a depth-10 verdict at 3-8 s on a phone with a 2-4 s warm-up). Add acceptance: with the Worker stubbed to never become ready, play('Nd4') in the tutorial holds within 100 ms and play('d3') does not.

Define the answer set and the category priority in one table, and make the tests and the prose agree. Per category: hanging_after_move: the enemy squares that can capture the piece, cheapest marked best; ignored_attack: the square of his own piece that their last move reached (as the Ruy acceptance expects), question 'Their last move reached one of yours. Tap it.'; free_piece_ignored: the free piece's square; allowed_mate: the square their mating piece lands on; missed_mate: the square his mating piece lands on. Priority: ignored_attack takes precedence over hanging_after_move whenever chess.js says the piece was attacked before his move (the chess-master's first look), and the core_loop 4 and gate.js lists must say so; today they say the opposite of the acceptance.
nice_to_change: Do not swap the question under his eyes. A 15-word serif line takes a beginner three or four seconds to read; the K1 reply lands at 1-1.5 s, in the middle of that read, and the 120 ms cross-fade replaces the words he is on. Either accept Claude's question only if it arrives within about 400 ms of the hold, or use K1 only for the follow-ups (if_right, if_partial, if_wrong) and the But... reply. And give K1 a job the template cannot do: let the fact sheet offer two looks (the pawn that takes, the piece he walked past) and let Claude pick the one his hold history says he skips most; the current example output is the template verbatim.

Make the 'Looked.' reward real and legible. The condition 'their last move newly attacked a piece of his and after his move nothing of his is hanging' fires on every harmless attack (in the placement line 6...Bg4 'attacks' the f3 knight, defended twice; any White move then earns a chip), so it rewards nothing; require that ignoring the attack would have lost two or more points (the ignored_attack precondition). And a 14 px grey chip for 1.2 s is invisible to someone looking at the board; put it in the serif line for the beat ('Looked. The bishop was on your knight.'). This is the only positive reinforcement for the chess-master's first look, and the hold alone only ever teaches it negatively.

Let him deliver the mate. Resigning at -900 removes the queen-and-king mate rep that chess-master.md puts in the under-1000 band, and 'Black gives up' is a weaker ending than 'Checkmate. Well played.' Have the bot play on when the material is a queen or a rook and the board is simple (few pieces, no bot counterplay), raise the resign threshold otherwise, and let category (d)'s 'You have a checkmate on the board. Tap the square.' do its work; stalemating a won position is a real under-1000 failure and worth one hold of its own ('Hold on. After this, can their king move at all?').

'But...' is not parseable in five seconds by someone who has never seen the product; it reads as a fragment. Try 'I had a plan…' or 'Hear me out' and let Sambudh's first session choose. Keep it a link, as specified.

The '-2' float assumes he knows piece values, which the brief says he has never studied. The first time a '-N' floats in a view, the serif line names it once in words ('A knight is worth about three pawns. You gave two away.'); after that the number alone.

Template copy is hard-wired to one case: (a) says 'Where does their queen land?' (build it from the mating piece's name), and the partial line 'Is there something cheaper? Look at the pawns.' makes no sense for Bxf7+ in the 6...d6 position where the recapturers are the rook and the king. Specify the template table by category x piece-name x whether a pawn is among the takers, and test it on all nine verified positions, not only Nxe5.

The tutorial undoes a good move ('Safe. Now try the one everyone plays: bishop takes f7.' slides his 4.d3 back), which punishes the exact habit the product exists to build, on screen one. Either let him keep the safe move and run the canned hold the first time Bxf7+ or Nxe5 appears in any game, or phrase the revert as praise that keeps the move ('Good. Keep that. Now, so you see what I do, try the one everyone plays').

The hanging_after_move test requires 'the engine's best reply is that capture'; when the opponent has something even better (a mate in two, a bigger fork) the hung piece is not held and he loses it a move later with no hand. Accept the capture if it is the first move of either multipv line of the reply search, with the depth-10 cp loss still required.

Budget the first game for his 10-15 minutes explicitly: measure plies per game and seconds per move pair in the self-play, and state in success_criteria that a first game ends (mate, resignation, give-up) inside 12 minutes at 15 s per human move.
critiques.strongest_part: The held move itself, and the fact that it is exactly the chess-master's curriculum turned into a thumb gesture. The four categories map one-to-one onto the under-1000 band's three looks plus the 'change chairs' check from lesson 0001 p3 (ignored_attack = what did their last move attack; free_piece_ignored = what can I take; allowed_mate and missed_mate = what checks are there; hanging_after_move = play it in your head and look from their chair), nothing outside that band ever holds, and the whole beat (lift, amber square, dimmed board, 'Hold on. ... Tap it.', graded by chess.js, 'Take it back' with no mark, 'Show me' with the ghost and the '-2') works with zero LLM calls and no reading beyond one sentence. The first screen is a board and one line, which a beginner parses in under five seconds, and 'Show me' is the best single piece of feedback in the spec: watching the future happen on your own board and then undo itself is understood by someone who has never heard the word centipawn. If the opponent is fixed so he can win and gets pieces to take, this core is the right thing to build.

refuted.claim: Thesis: "nothing in the world acts in that half-second the way a coach does: by stopping the hand and asking a question" and "the first chess software whose coaching happens where the rating is actually lost, in the player's hand."
refuted.why_wrong: Stopping the hand after a bad move, before the opponent replies, asking the player a question and offering a free take-back has shipped since 2018 in Dr. Wolf (now Chess.com's), which says the equivalent of "Are you certain?" after a hanging move and offers play-on or take-back; Shredder's coach "warns you if you are about to make a mistake"; Fritz's coach "appears and offers to help" on a blunder with a 'Coach is watching' toggle; Chessmaster 9000 (2002) "immediately notifies players of better moves when they move their pieces into danger." The spec's own incumbents paragraph omits Dr. Wolf and Shredder entirely. What no product found does is the one thing the spec should claim: the question is answered by a tap on the board, the answer is withheld, and the coach otherwise says nothing. 'First in the hand' is false; 'first whose question you answer on the board' is defensible.
refuted.evidence: PopSci hands-on (popsci.com/?p=568779): "Dr. Wolf politely asks after my rookie mistake of opening up my undefended pawn on e4 for capture... I can choose either to play on or to take back my move." Chess.com blog 'Meet Dr. Wolf' (chess.com/blog/Sawbonez/meet-dr-wolf-1). Shredder App Store listing (apps.apple.com/st/app/id308032437): "During the game a coach is watching your moves and warns you if you are about to make a mistake." Fritz 15 help (help.chessbase.com/fritz/15/eng/000082.htm): "If you make a blunder or a poor move, the coach appears and offers to help." Chessmaster 9000 press (worthplaying.com/article/2002/7/12/news/4679). Spec thesis paragraph lists only Chessmaster, Fritz, HIARCS, Lucas Chess, Play Coach.

refuted.claim: The incumbents that interrupt "tell you the move was bad or show you a better one" (thesis), with Chess.com Play Coach named among them.
refuted.why_wrong: Play Coach is described by Chess.com as withholding the move and pointing at pieces: "Coach doesn't just tell you what to play. It helps you understand the position and encourages you to look for the right answer"; hints "may highlight pieces to point you in the right direction"; it can "pose challenges for you"; you can "take back moves and try again." So 'withholds the move, lights pieces, lets you retry' is already in the market leader. The real differences are (a) Play Coach talks every move ("Move-by-move guidance – Get helpful commentary and tips every move") while Hold On is silent on clean moves, and (b) Play Coach does not suspend the move or grade a tap. The spec must state the difference at that resolution or a reviewer who has used Play Coach will read Hold On as Play Coach with the volume down.
refuted.evidence: chess.com/news/view/announcing-play-coach ("doesn't just tell you what to play... encourages you to look for the right answer"; "jump in whenever there's an opportunity for you to learn"); chess.com/announcements/view/new-play-coach ("commentary and tips every move"; "Hint button... highlight pieces"); support.chess.com/en/articles/10877257. Spec: thesis sentence 2 and the_new_interaction's 'three things'.

refuted.claim: Implicit in the thesis and in 'The hold' why_mvp: no existing product acts before the piece lands; the incumbents act after the move.
refuted.why_wrong: Three shipping products act while the piece is lifted: Fritz/ChessBase Assisted Analysis ("When you click on a piece, the consequences of a move to all possible target squares are evaluated and each evaluation is highlighted in colour... red a clear mistake"), the ChessUp physical board (touch a piece, candidate squares light green/blue/red), and the Chess.com Highlighter extension ("shows which squares are safe, attacked, or will leave your piece hanging before you make your move... training wheels for people new to the game"). They all show rather than ask, which is exactly the spec's differentiator, so the spec should cite them as the 'shows' camp and position the hold against them, not claim the half-second is empty.
refuted.evidence: help.chessbase.com/CBase/16/Eng/assisted_analysis.htm; Fritz 20/21 Handbook (books.chessbase.com/perma/c/681e1e44120628c0c650ee00); ChessUp help (chessup2-knowledge-base.helpscoutdocs.com/article/213) and playchessup.com; Chrome Web Store listing ijalkedcklihhankncgkeckaldbdncck.

refuted.claim: later_features: "'Sit in their chair'... The skeptic's strongest novelty claim."
refuted.why_wrong: Flipping the board after a blunder so the player sees it from the other side is a documented Dr. Wolf behaviour ("the feature where he recommends we flip sides after I make a blunder so I can better appreciate my mistake"). Having the player execute the capture with their own finger is a drill variant of that, not a new claim. Ranking it as the strongest novelty bet means iteration two would spend its headline on prior art.
refuted.evidence: chess.com/blog/Sawbonez/meet-dr-wolf-1 (reviewer on the side-switch suggestion); spec later_features[0] and open_questions[5].

refuted.claim: 'But...' (K2) is "the one place on the whole table where the LLM is load-bearing" and "the market skeptic's genuinely new idea."
refuted.why_wrong: Typing a free-form question about the move in front of you and getting a Stockfish-grounded LLM answer with squares drawn already exists: Chessiro ("Type a question about the move in front of you and you get an answer about that exact position — and the coach draws arrows on the board", Stockfish 18 in-browser) and the 'AI Chess Coach' Chrome extension ("ask your coach anything in natural language" on Chess.com/Lichess). What is new in Hold On is only the placement (inside a suspended move) and the shape (answers a stated plan, ends with a question, names no move). But as specced the K2 reply's closing question is rhetorical: nothing computes its answer set and no tap is graded, which is the spec's own definition of 'a chatbot next to a board' ("the answer to its question is a tap on the board"). As written, K2 is a one-shot chat bubble with a nice placement.
refuted.evidence: chessiro.com/blog/inside-chessiro-game-review and chessiro.com/faq; extscope.org/extension/jbfgbfnhbdgmpgpekjnipjhgpgaacflp (AI Chess Coach extension); spec K2 description ('end with one question that names no move... up to three squares lit') and acceptance (asserts only text equality and 'lit' classes, never a graded tap).

refuted.claim: 'Tap-to-answer' why_mvp: "Answering on the board is what turns a warning into a look the player did himself; it is the difference between this and Fritz."
refuted.why_wrong: Fritz already has tap-the-answer, as a training mode: "Attack – here you are required to click all white and black pieces that can be captured by the enemy; Defence – click all squares which are not defended by at least one friendly piece." The difference is not the tap; it is doing the tap inside a live game, on the move the player was about to play, with the engine choosing the moment. The spec should say that, because 'tap the attacker' as a drill is twenty years old (Steps Method workbooks, ChessKid 'find the hanging piece', Fritz training).
refuted.evidence: Fritz 20 Handbook training section (books.chessbase.com/perma/c/681e1e44120628c0c650eeb9); chesskid.com/learn/articles/is-it-hanging-or-protected; Steps Method Step 1 (stappenmethode.nl, cited by lesson 0001 source block at /home/user/hello-world/chess-study/lessons/0001-blunder-check.yml).

refuted.claim: The opponent "plays like an 800" / "plays like a person at his level."
refuted.why_wrong: An engine that deliberately makes human-shaped mistakes is prior art (Shredder: "at weaker settings it is programmed to deliberately make typical human mistakes"; Maia1 trained on 10M 1100-rated games "still makes a lot of human-like blunders"; Noctie trained on a billion Lichess games), and those do it from human data rather than an 80 cp sampler with a one-in-eight gift timer. The spec cannot claim likeness to an 800 with zero self-play evidence; it can claim a designed behaviour: 'hangs a minor piece on purpose about once a game and punishes every piece you hang.' Say that, and move 'like an 800' to the open questions where the spec already admits it is a guess.
refuted.evidence: apps.apple.com/st/app/id308032437 (Shredder); lichess.org/blog/X9PUixUAANCqFRSh/introducing-maia; maiachess.com; spec thesis ('an opponent that plays like an 800'), core_loop[9], open_questions[2] ('are guesses at an 800-strength opponent').

must_change: Rewrite the novelty claim in thesis, tagline and the_new_interaction to what the evidence supports and nothing more: 'the only chess software that suspends your move, asks a question you answer by tapping the board, never names the answer or the move, and otherwise says nothing.' Add the missing incumbents to the thesis paragraph with one clause each on what they do and the one thing they do not: Dr. Wolf (interrupts, asks 'Are you certain?', take-back, flip sides; names the problem, yes/no answer), Shredder and Fritz coach (warn and offer help; show the move), Fritz Assisted Analysis / ChessUp / Chess.com Highlighter (colour squares before the drop; show, do not ask), Play Coach (withholds the move, lights pieces, retries; talks every move, nothing is held), Chessiro (typed question grounded by Stockfish with arrows; after the game). Delete the words 'first' and 'nothing in the world'.

Make K2 ('But...') a board question or cut it from the MVP. The reply contract becomes {say, ask: {kind, squares}} where kind is one of a small enumerated set whose answer set facts.js has already computed from chess.js (e.g. 'square_the_held_piece_can_reach_that_attacks_target_and_no_pawn_reaches', 'piece_that_takes_on_square', 'what_takes_back'); the prompt lists the kinds available for this hold with their answer sets; validate.js rejects a reply whose kind is not offered or whose answer set is empty; the tap after a K2 reply is graded by chess.js exactly like K1's. Acceptance must include a graded tap after a K2 reply, not only text equality. Without this, K2 is the 'chatbot next to a board' the spec says it rejects, and the one LLM-load-bearing moment is a chat bubble.

Replace the later_features novelty ranking: 'Sit in their chair' is Dr. Wolf's flip-sides feature and must not be presented as 'the skeptic's strongest novelty claim'. Name the real bet, which the brief's own 'not in the world' sentence already points at ('a memory of what you personally keep getting wrong'): the question that remembers, i.e. K1 choosing which look to point at from this player's hold log and phrasing it as 'This one again' (currently iteration three), promoted to iteration two with the hold log it already has. That is the only item on the list no incumbent covers.

Make the silence testable, because silence is the real contrast with Play Coach ('commentary and tips every move') and Dr. Wolf (praise and commentary). The spec's thesis says the coach says nothing on ninety percent of moves, yet 'Looked.' fires every time the opponent attacks something and he saves it, and 'Free knight. You looked.' on every free capture; in a beginner game that can be a third of his moves. Add a quiet budget to success_criteria and a scenario: over a scripted 30-move game with no holds, the coach line and chip change at most N times (pick N, e.g. 4), and the chip never fires twice in a row. Otherwise the differentiator evaporates in play and the product becomes Dr. Wolf with better typography.
nice_to_change: Cite lesson 0001 ('p3: Before you let go of the piece: the same three looks, from their chair', /home/user/hello-world/chess-study/lessons/0001-blunder-check.yml) as the source of the hold's pedagogy and of every tutorial and acceptance position; it strengthens the story that the hold is a verified lesson turned into an interaction rather than an invention, and the depth-20 verification comments there are the evidence the thesis cites.

Position the tap against Fritz's 'Attack/Defence: click all pieces that can be captured' training mode explicitly: 'the drill, inside your own game, on the move you were about to play, at the moment you were about to play it'. This is the most honest and most persuasive sentence available and it is not in the spec.

Drop 'plays like an 800' from copy and docs until the self-play tuning in risks[1] exists; add a measurable opponent target to success_criteria (e.g. in 100 headless self-play games against a fixed 1000-ish sampler, the bot hangs a minor piece in at least 60 percent of games and never hangs its queen), and note Shredder/Maia/Noctie as the prior art for human-shaped mistakes so nobody later markets the gift rule as new.

'Show me' is a presentation of what Game Review's 'Show Lost Piece', Lucas Chess's tutor window and Dr. Wolf's explanation already do; the ghost-then-rewind on his own board is good execution, so keep it, but make sure no copy or doc calls it new.

Run validate.js's SAN and banned-word rules over the template table in the build (extend copy_check.js), since 'the coach never names the move' is now the novelty claim and the templates are where a stray 'Nxe5' or 'the pawn on d6' can leak before the second wrong tap.

For the share link in iteration two, the novel object is the held question travelling with the position (Lichess and Chess.com already share positions and puzzles); write the feature's one line around the question, not the position.

Consider rotating K1's look across categories by history (open_questions[3]) in the MVP prompt rather than later: it costs nothing, it is the one thing a template table cannot do, and it is the cheapest proof that Claude is load-bearing in K1 at all.
critiques.strongest_part: The held move whose answer is a tap: the engine decides the moment, the piece does not land, the question withholds the answer square, chess.js grades the tap instantly, and Claude only phrases. I searched for a product that asks 'what takes it? Tap it.' on a suspended move in a live game and found none; Dr. Wolf asks yes/no and names the problem, Play Coach lights the pieces for you, Fritz offers the tap only as a training drill, and the square-colouring products show rather than ask. Combined with 'zero sample calls in a clean game' and a validator that makes a wrong square physically unable to reach the board, that is a genuinely new interaction and not a chat box; the spec's problem is that it wraps this true claim in several false ones.
