page_tools.name: (none in the MVP)
page_tools.purpose: Every fact Claude needs is in the prompt; each tool round would be another request inside a beat that must feel like a beat, and the grading of every tap is the page's own.

page_tools.name: show_position (iteration three, 'Read my game')
page_tools.purpose: Sets the board to a ply of THIS game only (the page refuses any ply outside the move list) with optional highlight squares, so the viewer watches the coach move through the game while it writes.
page_tools.returns: 'ok' or throws 'Error: ply out of range'

page_tools.name: check (iteration three, 'Read my game')
page_tools.purpose: Returns the in-page engine's evaluation and best reply for a candidate move at a given ply at depth 12, so every claim in the review is grounded before it is written.

llm_design.grounding_rule: Two gates, one before and one after, and no tools in the beat. Before: facts.js computes the fact sheet from chess.js and the Worker (the held move, what takes it and what takes back with piece names, the net loss, the category, the answer squares, the looks available for this hold with their answer sets kept page-side, the squares that may be named, the pieces on them) and the prompt contains nothing else; Claude never evaluates a move, never decides whether to hold, never types a FEN, and never asks a question the page cannot grade, because the question after a K2 reply is the page's own words for a look chess.js computed. After: validate.js is an ordered pipeline: (1) every [a-h][1-8] token must be in the allowed set (K1: the fact-sheet squares, and never an answer square inside if_wrong; K2: the fact-sheet squares, every occupied square and the held piece's legal destinations), and a piece word before 'on <square>' must match the piece chess.js has there; those tokens are then masked; (2) on the masked text a SAN-shaped token (a piece letter, an 'x', an '=' or O-O) outside the listed moves rejects; (3) any remaining digit rejects; (4) blunder, mistake, inaccuracy, '??' (assembled from char codes) reject; (5) word and sentence caps, a question mark in K2's say, an ask outside the offered set, or more than three squares reject. The spec's two example outputs pass this pipeline (checked by a unit test), which the old regex failed. A rejected reply is replaced by the template silently and window.__coachRejects increments. Grading of every tap uses chess.js's own answer set; Claude's text is only ever words on the line and marks on squares that exist in the fact sheet.
llm_design.without_claude: Identical game minus one link. When claude.use('sample') settles null (any browser outside the viewer, local testing, a friend's copy), when the viewer declines, or on any error: the gate fires exactly the same, the lifted piece and the amber square appear, the template question for the category shows, the tap is graded by chess.js with template follow-ups built from piece names, Show me plays the refutation, both buttons work, the close card shows the counts, and the next game opens with the templated remembered line. 'Hear me out' is simply absent, no control is ever shown disabled, and no message mentions Claude.

final.engine_design: Stockfish 18 lite (app/vendor/stockfish-18-lite-single.js + .wasm, 7.3 MB, single-threaded; its uci output lists Threads, Hash, MultiPV, Skill Level 0-20, UCI_LimitStrength, UCI_Elo 1320-3190, confirmed this session) in one Web Worker created at load and warmed with uci, isready and ucinewgame, behind engine.js: a serialized command queue with search ids, an info-line parser (depth, multipv, score cp or mate, pv), search(fen, {depth, multipv, skill}) resolving with per-line scores, pvs and the bestmove, and stop() marking the current id stale so its late bestmove is discarded; a new go is sent only after the previous bestmove has arrived (the engine ignores a go mid-search). chess.js 1.4.0 does everything instantaneous: legality, SAN and UCI, FEN, game over, moves({verbose: true}) for dots and rings, attackers() per square (it reports defenders too, verified in the vendored source) for the fact sheet, isStalemate, and the mate-in-one and hanging-piece enumerations the bot's guards use. All evaluations are converted to the player's side (mate N maps to +/-(10000-N)). The schedule per move pair: (1) IDLE, player to move: setoption Skill Level 20; ucinewgame; go depth 14 multipv 2 on the current FEN as the pre-search (depth 12 took 11-243 ms in the probe), yielding evalBefore, the best move, whether it is a free capture or a mate in one. (2) On drop: stop (a stop 50 ms into the pre-search still returned depth 10 in 92 ms; if the stopped depth is under 8 a go depth 10 runs first), chess.js applies the move on a scratch board and builds the post-move facts synchronously, then go depth 12 multipv 2 on the post-move FEN (depth 10 took 1-42 ms; budget under 150 ms headless, under 600 ms on a mid-range phone); evalAfter is negated to the player's side, the reply and whether it is a capture, check or mate 1 come from line 1, and hanging_after_move also accepts the capture as the first move of line 2. (3) gate.js verdict. (4) Clean: commit; the opponent's move as in bot.js (full-strength depth 8 multipv 2 look, then the gift enumeration with up to six depth-10 checks, then Skill Level 3 go depth 2 with chess.js guards), all well under 300 ms headless and shown no sooner than 400 ms after his move so it reads as a move; then back to (1). Held: no search runs while the hold is open; Take it back reuses the cached pre-search; Play it anyway runs Skill Level 20 go depth 12 for the true best reply. Cold engine: while the Worker has not answered readyok, the player's moves commit with no verdict and no reward, and the bot's reply comes from the book or waits with a 6 px dot and 'Warming up the other side...' at the opponent's edge; the tutorial never touches the engine. Resignation: bot-side eval at or below -900 for three consecutive bot moves after move six, except when the player has a queen or rook and the bot has only king and pawns. Show me: the ghost line is the reply pv's first one or two plies, played from a scratch Chess; the '-N' is chess.js's material difference across those plies. Determinism: ucinewgame before every pre-search, Hash left at 16 MB; the probe's run-to-run drift was 15-25 cp and every test position has at least 70 cp of margin. The whole thirteen-pair acceptance batch ran in 1.9 s in headless Chromium with a 368 ms warm-up. Every number the gate uses, every refutation Show me plays, every answer square the tap is graded against, every gift the bot leaves and every fact in Claude's prompt comes from this pipeline; the engine never speaks to the player and Claude never evaluates a position.

information_architecture.contents: The board on the verified Italian after 3...Nf6, White at the bottom; the serif line 'Try one. Most people take the pawn in front of the king here. Go on.'; an empty link row; an empty action bar; a 44 px header with 'Hold On' small at left and, at right, the 'Give up' link and the theme dot (a 12 px circle, filled --ink in light, hollow in dark, 44 px target; unset follows the system until the first tap).
information_architecture.primary_action: Make a move (tap a piece, tap a square).

information_architecture.contents: The board with the last move tinted; the line 'Your move.' (or, at the start of games two onward, the remembered line); an empty action bar; occasionally, within the quiet budget, the green ring with 'Free knight. You looked.' or 'You looked. The pawn was on your bishop.' for two seconds.
The piece on its new square at full opacity, input locked, nothing drawn; a faint dot on the piece only if the verdict takes longer than 250 ms (a code path, not a tested state).

The piece lifted with a shadow over the destination, the destination breathing amber, every other square dimmed; the line 'Hold on. ...' with one question whose answer is a square; the link row with 'Show me' and, when available, 'Hear me out'; the action bar EMPTY.
information_architecture.primary_action: Tap the square you think answers the question.

information_architecture.contents: The same board with the tapped square ringed green (right or partial) or the hint line (wrong; after a second wrong tap the answer square glows and is named); the action bar now holds [Take it back] (ink, focused) and [Play it anyway]; the first hold a browser sees adds 'Take it back costs nothing; play it anyway is real.'
information_architecture.primary_action: Take it back (primary) or Play it anyway.

information_architecture.contents: Real pieces at 35 percent, ghost pieces playing the capture at 50 percent, the 28 px serif '-N' rising from his board edge (named once in words the first time), a beat, then everything slides back to the hold.

A one-line input in the action bar with placeholder 'Say what you were going for', a send button and the note about the browser's one-time question; the board scaled to stay visible above the keyboard. On send: his words echo in muted ink under 'Looking...'; if this is the view's first call the platform's consent dialog sits over this stable state (sub-state 'asking permission'); then the coach's two sentences with up to three squares corner-marked, followed by the page's question for the chosen look; the input gone; the next tap graded.
information_architecture.primary_action: Type one line and send; then tap the square the page asks for.

information_architecture.contents: The board with the player's move committed; the line unchanged; the reply slides in between 400 ms and 1 s; a 6 px --muted dot at the opponent's board edge after 800 ms, and 'Warming up the other side...' as a 12 px caption there only when a bot move is truly waiting on engine warm-up.
The opponent's capture slides in; one honest sentence in the line ('There it goes. A knight for a pawn. You saw it coming; that counts.' or '... Next time, the pawns first.'); back to Your move.

After three moves at -900 or worse, once: the line 'This one is gone. Start again?' with [Start again] [Keep playing] in the action bar; or, from the header's 'Give up' link at any time, 'Give up this one? [Yes] [Keep playing]'.

The final position; the line 'Checkmate. Well played.' / 'That one got away.' / 'Black gives up. You are a rook and a bishop ahead and it knows it.' / 'You gave up.' / 'A draw.'; the close card under the board: 'I stopped your hand 3 times; you took it back twice. Pieces given away: 1 (last game 4). Free pieces you took: 2.' with one caption line per hold in piece words; one button [Again].

information_architecture.screen_or_state: Coach unavailable (sample null, declined, or an error)
information_architecture.contents: Nothing visibly different: the same holds with template questions and follow-ups, the same Show me and buttons; the 'Hear me out' link is absent; after rate_limited the line says 'Coach is resting.' for a minute.

visual_direction.mood: A tournament hall, not an app: a vinyl board on a quiet table, a coach beside you who speaks in a book's serif and otherwise says nothing. Calm, warm where the board is, cool everywhere else. The only movement on the page is pieces moving; the only colour that ever raises its voice is the amber of a held square. Relief, not shame: nothing on this page is ever red, there is no bar, no label, no score, no card grid. It should look like chess to a person who has never seen an AI product and like craft to a person who has.
visual_direction.palette: Tokens on :root, redefined under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) guarded by :root:not([data-theme=light]) and again under :root[data-theme=dark], with an explicit body background. Light: --bg #f3f4f1; --ink #1f2430; --muted #6b7280; --coach #243b6b (the serif line and the primary button); --on-coach #ffffff; --hold #c98a1b (amber); --ok #4f7a4a (used only for a right tap and a free piece taken); --square-light #e9e5d8; --square-dark #8f9a7e; --tint rgba(36,59,107,.22) for the last move; --dim rgba(0,0,0,.12) for the hold's dimmed squares; --piece-white #f4f1e6 with outline #2a2a2a; --piece-black #2b2b2b with edge #f4f1e6. Dark: --bg #141821; --ink #e6e8ee; --muted #9aa3b2; --coach #9db4e8; --on-coach #141821; --hold #e0a53a; --ok #7fae78; --square-light #b8b4a0; --square-dark #5c6b5a; --tint rgba(157,180,232,.28); --dim rgba(0,0,0,.28), so a held board gets darker in both themes and the board stays the warmest, brightest object on the page. The amber hold glow is a box-shadow inset, never a fill, so pieces stay legible on it.
visual_direction.type: The coach's line in Source Serif 4 (Google Fonts; fallback Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif) at 19 px / 1.35 on phone and 21 px on desktop, regular weight, sentence case, in a box fixed at four lines (103 px phone, 113 px desktop) in every state so the board never moves; copy caps keep everything inside it (template questions at most 16 words, K2 say 20 words plus an 8-word question, K1 lines 20 words; measured: 28 words fill three lines at 368 px in a serif narrower than Source Serif 4, so four lines is the margin). Labels, buttons, counts and the header in IBM Plex Sans (fallback system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif) at 14 px, medium weight, sentence case, no uppercase tracking; the player's echoed words in the serif at 19 px in --muted. The '-N' float in the serif at 28 px; board coordinates in Plex Sans at 11 px. Never Inter, never a display font, never bold serif headlines; the page has no headline at all.
visual_direction.board: A static 64-cell CSS grid, square, width min(100vw - 32px, 62vh) (46 px squares at 400 px; at 400 x 800 the header 44, line 103, links 24, board 368 and action bar 56 total 595 px, so nothing scrolls), 1 px --muted border at 20 percent, 4 px radius, coordinates inside the a-file and first-rank squares in the opposite square tint. Pieces: twelve flat silhouettes built to the construction rule in 'The board' (ivory with a 1.5 px ink outline, charcoal with a 1 px ivory edge), each a focusable button on an absolutely positioned layer moved by transform. Overlays, back to front: last-move tint; legal dots (10 px, ink at 35 percent) and capture rings (2 px); the hold dim (--dim on every square but the destination); the amber inset glow on the destination; the green ring for a right tap and a free capture; the answer glow after a second wrong tap (amber fill at 25 percent); Claude's marked squares as four small --coach corner marks, never a fourth ring colour; the ghost piece layer at 50 percent above the real layer, which drops to 35 percent during Show me. The held piece: translateY(-6px) scale(1.06) with a 0 8px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.28) shadow, full opacity, visibly off the square. Above the board: the 44 px header ('Hold On' small, left; 'Give up' in --muted and the theme dot, right). Under the line: a 24 px link row whose links have 44 px tap targets. Below the board: a 56 px action bar that is empty until a decision is needed, with one ink primary button and one quiet secondary. No move list, no eval bar, no clock, no rating, no settings gear on the first frame.
visual_direction.motion: Pieces slide 150 ms ease-out by transform; a picked-up piece scales to 1.06 with a shadow in 100 ms; the amber hold breathes on a 1.6 s inset-glow loop; the opponent's reply slides no sooner than 400 ms after his move; Show me plays 600 ms per ply, the '-N' rises 24 px and fades over 700 ms, a 500 ms beat, then a 300 ms rewind; the take-back slide is the same 150 ms as a move; the green ring holds 900 ms; a reward line stays 2 s; 'Looking...' pulses on a 1 s loop. Under prefers-reduced-motion every duration is 0, the breathe becomes a static amber ring, the float becomes a static 28 px label beside the board for 1.2 s, and Show me shows the final ghost position statically. Nothing bounces, nothing slides in from off-screen, no confetti.
visual_direction.what_to_avoid: An eval bar, a move list, a rating, a clock, a '??' or 'Blunder' label, anything red, a speech bubble or chat balloon, a standing chat box, a settings gear or strength slider on the first frame, a dashboard of stats, rounded cards everywhere, the cream-and-terracotta or acid-green-on-black or purple-gradient AI defaults, Inter, emoji anywhere, uppercase tracked labels, Unicode chess glyphs as pieces, a hollow 'empty state' screen, a tutorial overlay with arrows and tooltips, a question that changes under the reader, a disabled control, a sentence that claims he saw something he did not, and any copy that addresses the player as a user ('Submit', 'Analyze', 'Accuracy').

final.persistence: store.js exposes {get, set, append, list} and in the MVP is backed by localStorage only, every read and write wrapped in try/catch so a private window or blocked storage still plays: holdon.v1.tutorialSeen ('1'), holdon.v1.firstHoldSeen ('1'), holdon.v1.firstFloatSeen ('1'), holdon.v1.theme ('light' | 'dark' | unset, set by the header dot and written to data-theme on :root), holdon.v1.giftRate (the current notch), holdon.v1.games (the last five game summaries: {id, date, result, givenAway, holds: [{fen, san, category, taps, outcome, coachShown}], freeTaken, playedAnyway, plies}), holdon.v1.holds (the last thirty hold moments across games, the material for the remembered line and, in iteration two, for the question that remembers, 'Play it again from here' and 'Send this one'). Consent is per view and is never stored. Nothing about the current game is persisted mid-game (a reload starts a new game). Iteration two moves games and holds to the db + user capabilities at data/users/{self}/games and data/users/{self}/holds behind the same store.js interface, with localStorage kept as a mirror, because localStorage is per browser and Sambudh will switch from laptop to phone; the builder reads the artifact-capabilities skill for db's exact API before writing that path, noting that viewers of a public link who are not the owner never write.
success_criteria: In headless Chromium (scripts/app_check.js with scripts/scenarios/holdon.js): every acceptance scenario above passes in one exported function in under three minutes, report.ok is true at 1280 px and 400 px in light and dark with zero console errors, zero page errors, zero failed requests and no horizontal overflow; the same run with --no-stub passes with [data-action=but] absent.

The gate is right on every verified position: it holds on Nxe5 and Bxf7+ (both Italian positions), O-O in the Ruy as ignored_attack, Nc3 after 4...Nxe4, Nbd2 in the placement position, O-O after 5...Ng4, g4 after 1.f3 e5 and Qh3 in the Scholar's position, and stays silent on h3, d3, Ba4, dxe4, hxg4 (both positions) and Qxf7#; the tutorial table holds Bxf7+, Nxe5, Nd4, Ba6 and Be6 and nothing else; a clean six-move sequence makes zero sample calls.

The opponent is measured, not described: python3 scripts/bot_sim.py 10 reports at least 2 verified gifts per game, mean game length at most 100 plies, no sampled move that hangs a rook or queen or allows mate in one, a score of 5 to 9 of 10 against Stockfish at UCI_Elo 1320 and at most 2 of 10 against the same engine prevented from leaving a piece hanging (this session: 8/10 and 0.5/10 with seven bot resignations).

The beat holds: drop to verdict under 300 ms in headless Chromium and under 600 ms on a mid-range phone; the template question is on screen at 0 ms of every hold; the opponent replies between 400 ms and 1 s on non-gift moves; the tutorial and the player's own first move never wait on engine warm-up.

Claude is never wrong on the board: every stub reply that names an off-list square, a wrong piece on a square, a SAN token, a digit, a banned word, an unoffered ask or an answer square inside a hint is rejected (window.__coachRejects increments) and the template shows; the two example outputs in this spec pass the validator; no square is ever marked that is not in the fact sheet; every question after a K2 reply is graded by chess.js.
Silence is measured: a scripted 20-move clean game changes the coach line at most four times outside holds and never on consecutive player moves.

Sambudh, in his first session: understands the first screen without a word of instruction, reaches a real game within 45 s having seen a hold and both buttons without any dialog, finishes a game inside twelve minutes (mate, resignation, give-up, or start-again; the recipe's 97 plies per game at 15 s per human move), takes back at least one hold, takes at least one free piece, presses Hear me out at least once, and his second game ends with fewer pieces given away than his first.

The mission's own measure, over the first week: three of five games with zero pieces given away, read off the close card's count, with the hold firing less often from game to game and the bot resigning in the games where it happens.

Scope discipline holds: the shipped page contains no eval bar, move list, rating, clock, standing chat box, red colour, '??', or the words blunder, mistake, inaccuracy, Submit, Analyze, Accuracy or user, and no template or marketing line claims the product is first, new, or that the opponent plays like an 800 (the copy test enforces the words; the thesis above is the claim).

Cost: a typical game spends at most the Hear me out calls the player chose to make plus two to five K1 calls after consent, each under 2 KB, none with tools, none from a timer or loop, and the consent dialog appears only over a held state on an explicit tap.
risks: Over-holding turns the coach into a nag: the thresholds (200 cp AND a capture or mate refutation AND a chess.js-nameable mechanism AND net two points) are enforced by the scenario tests, never by taste; the quiet-after-two rule with its mate and five-point exceptions and the never-the-same-square rule ship on day one.

The opponent is now measured against an engine, not against a person: Skill Level 3 at depth 2 may still play moves that look alien, the gift enumeration may rarely qualify in closed positions, and against a player who hangs more than three pieces a game the punish-always rule wins almost every game early (a 1320 engine scored 2 of 10). The design's answer is the hold itself, the mercy offer and the give-up link; Sambudh's first three games and scripts/bot_sim.py decide SKILL, SAMPLE_DEPTH and GIFT_RATE, which are three named constants.

Engine warm-up on a slow phone is 2-4 s plus a 7.3 MB download: the tutorial and the book cover it, but the first real verdict on a cellular connection may be skipped by the cold-engine policy, and the verdict budget must be measured on a real Android, not only in headless Chromium.

Consent lands on the first Hear me out of every view; a viewer who declines never sees Claude for the rest of that view, and a viewer who never presses the link never sees Claude at all. That is accepted: the product plays identically, and the first week's coachShown counts say whether the words are missed.

The quick tier may ignore the rules (name an unlisted square, add a number, ask its own question); the validator and the template make this invisible, but a high rejection rate would mean Claude never speaks; measure window.__coachRejects on real calls and tighten the prompt rather than loosen the validator.

K1 is the weakest moment on the table: after consent it costs a call per hold for follow-up phrasing the template already does adequately; if the log shows it is rarely shown before his tap or rarely better, it is cut in iteration two and the call budget goes to the question that remembers.

Typing on a phone: the keyboard covers the board unless the board scales with visualViewport (unverifiable in headless Chromium); the fixed four-line box and the 20-plus-8-word cap are measured only with a stand-in serif, so the first phone screenshot with Source Serif 4 loaded must confirm no clipping.

The twelve silhouettes are two hours capped; if they are not legible at 46 px in the screenshots, the cburnett set ships with attribution and its CC BY-SA terms are noted beside the GPL engine in app/LICENSE.md.

localStorage is per browser: the close card's 'last game' and the remembered line vanish when he moves from laptop to phone; db + user must follow in iteration two before the memory story is promised in copy.

Scope creep toward Lichess: an eval bar, a move list, a strength slider and a rating are each one argument away; the copy test and the information architecture are the defence. Licensing: shipping Stockfish (GPLv3) means the page's own source should be published under a GPL-compatible licence; flagged in app/LICENSE.md, not solved.
open_questions: Does the opponent feel like a person to Sambudh? Skill Level 3 at depth 2 with chess.js guards is measured against an engine only; his first three games decide whether SKILL, SAMPLE_DEPTH or GIFT_RATE move, and whether a game that ends by mercy at move twenty feels like a loss or a lesson.

Is the tutorial's dare ('Try one. Most people take the pawn in front of the king here.') welcome or patronising on a second viewing by someone who already plays? It appears once per browser; the fallback is the plainer 'Your move. The first three moves are the usual ones.'

Does Hear me out get pressed at all on a phone, and when it is, does Claude's answer plus the page's graded question beat the template answer in a blind comparison on the same twenty holds? If not, the link stays and the LLM leaves it; if yes, it is the headline of the share link in iteration two.
Is one K1 call per hold after consent worth its cost? The hold log's coachShown field answers this after a week; the cut is already named in risks.

Which look does he actually skip most, and how many games of log does the question that remembers need before it is better than a coin flip? The hold log answers this after five games and decides iteration two's prompt.

Should the bot play on in every won position so he gets the mate rep, or only when it has king and pawns? The current rule is the narrow one for his 10-15 minutes; his first stalemate hold ('After this, can their king move at all?') will tell whether the queen-and-king mate belongs in the MVP's game.
Which licence for the page's own source, given the GPLv3 engine inside it; and does the piece set we draw get released with it?
changelog: Novelty claims rewritten (thesis, tagline, the_new_interaction, later_features): deleted 'first', 'nothing in the world' and 'plays like an 800'; added Dr. Wolf, Shredder, Fritz coach and Assisted Analysis, ChessUp, the Chess.com Highlighter, Play Coach, Chessiro, Maia and Noctie with one clause each on what they do and do not; the supportable claim is now the only claim; lesson 0001 p3 is cited as the pedagogy source. Reason: the novelty critic's evidence.

The opponent rebuilt and measured instead of described: gift candidates enumerated with chess.js over all legal moves (not inside the six best lines, where they never were), gifts from the bot's third move for the whole game, the sampler changed from an 80 cp window to Skill Level 3 at depth 2 with chess.js guards, the forced-capture rule written as one sentence (capture leading by 150 cp or mate), resignation widened with the king-and-pawns exception; eight recipes self-played ten games each against Stockfish at UCI_Elo 1320 plain and 'held' (scratchpad bot_sim2-5.py); the chosen recipe's numbers and the smoke script are in the spec. Reason: the beginner critic's six-game run (6-0, zero gifts) and this session's runs.

Gate category table rewritten with one discriminator (which piece the reply captures), ignored_attack placed before hanging_after_move with 'already' and 'lost its guard' sub-cases, allowed_stalemate added, the reply capture accepted from either of two reply lines, the answer and partial sets defined per category in one place, and the two-play-anyway silence given mate, stalemate and five-point exceptions. Reason: feasibility and beginner critics showed the old priority made the Ruy acceptance unreachable and the silence rule dangerous.

validate.js specified as an ordered pipeline (squares checked and masked, piece-word-on-square verified, SAN needing a piece letter or 'x' or '=' or O-O, digits, banned words from char codes, caps) and the allowed set widened for K2 to every occupied square and the held piece's destinations; a unit test on the spec's own examples added. Reason: the old regex rejected every example output in the spec (feasibility and design critics ran it).

Hear me out (was 'But...') became a graded board question: the reply is {say, ask, squares}, the ask is one of the looks chess.js computed for this hold, the page appends its own question for it and grades the next tap. Reason: the novelty critic's must-change; without it the one load-bearing LLM moment was a chat bubble.

Consent moved off the gate: K1 never fires before a view has consented through Hear me out, so the platform dialog appears only on an explicit tap over a stable held state, with copy under the input that explains it; an IA state for it added. Reason: consent is per view (sample.d.ts), so the old design put a modal over the lifted piece on the first hold of every session.

K1 reduced to follow-ups: it no longer writes or swaps the question (a quick reply lands mid-read), it returns if_right/if_partial/if_wrong/and_then/anyway used only after his tap, and it is explicitly secondary with a named cut condition. Reason: design and beginner critics on the mid-read swap and on K1 not earning its place.

Tutorial made engine-independent and complete: data/tutorial.json classifies all 33 legal moves from a depth-20 table computed this session (five held with answer sets, including Nd4, Ba6 and Be6 that the old table would have called safe); a safe move now stands and the game continues; the dare is in piece words; the first-hold explanation and the first-float naming are one-time lines. Reason: the old text contradicted itself ('gate runs as normal' vs 'canned') and undid good moves.

The two previously unverified positions (1.f3 e5 g4; Scholar's White to move) verified this session with scripts/engine_check.py at depth 20/24 and recorded in data/positions.json. Reason: the repo-verification claim was false for them.

Hold interaction: the action bar stays empty until he has tapped or 8 s pass; the Play it anyway sentence branches on his taps; ignored_attack's copy and grader agree (his attacked piece is the answer, the attacker is partial); the links have one home (a 24 px row under the line); the line box is fixed at four lines with measured word caps; the '-N' is 28 px. Reason: the design critic's measurements and the one-primary-action rule.

Rewards restated in FEN-derivable terms with the ignored_attack precondition, moved from a 14 px chip into the serif line, and put under a quiet budget (four per game, never consecutive) with a scenario. Reason: load(fen) has no 'last move'; silence is the real contrast with Play Coach and must be testable.
Give up link, the mercy offer, draw copy and material-in-words resignation added. Reason: self-play shows his losses are early and hopeless; without a way out the close card never appears.

Theme-safe tokens added (--dim as a black overlay in both themes, a dark --tint, --on-coach), Claude's marked squares as corner marks, the theme dot and the opponent's-edge dot defined, coordinates 11 px Plex Sans. Reason: the design critic's dark-mode and ring-ambiguity findings.

Scope cut for one session: tap-tap only, auto-queen promotion, eight-line book, text captions instead of mini boards on the close card, piece set with a written construction rule and a two-hour cap with cburnett as the fallback. Reason: the feasibility critic's cut list.

Test plan reconciled with scripts/app_check.js: one exported scenario function, the stub extended with an outcome field and window.__stubErrors consumed by the stub, the bot-as-White test replaced by Black-to-move positions, window.__app.fast and botMove added, the copy guard excluding validate.js and scenario fixtures and extended to Submit/Analyze/Accuracy/user, a node unit test for the pure gate. Reason: the feasibility and design critics read the harness.

Latency budget re-based on the probe (verdict 1-42 ms, pre-search 11-243 ms, warm-up 368 ms): verdict depth raised to 12, pre-search to 14, ucinewgame before each pre-search for determinism, a 400 ms minimum before the opponent's reply, the pending dot kept as an untested code path, a cold-engine policy stated. Reason: the old numbers were 10-50x too pessimistic and the real latency item (warm-up on a phone) had no policy.
decisions_rejected: Feasibility: ship GIFT_RATE at 0 until a 20-game headless smoke exists. Rejected: a bot that gives nothing teaches only defence (zero gifts in six games under the old rule; 10-0 with seven early resignations when gifts were switched off in this session's s3d2g0 run), and the smoke already exists and takes 25 seconds, so it is part of the definition of done and the constant ships at 0.12.

Beginner: calibrate over 100 self-play games with the bot scoring at most 40 percent against UCI_Elo 1320. Scaled down and redirected: ten games per recipe is what fits a session, and the measured fact is that the score against a piece-hanging 1320 is dominated by punish-always (every recipe scored 7-8.5 of 10), so the acceptance targets what matters to the design instead: verified gifts per game, game length, the guards, and at most 2 of 10 against a 1320 that never hangs a piece.

Beginner and feasibility: widen the sampler to a 250 cp window. Rejected after measuring: the flat 250 cp window produced 143-ply aimless games (adjudicated at the cap) with no gain in gifts; Skill Level 3 at depth 2, which the beginner critic also offered, gives 97-ply games and the same gift rate.

Design: open the Hear me out reply in the 56 px action-bar area instead of the line. Rejected: the serif line is the coach's only voice and a second place for words is the chat-bubble look; the line box is fixed at four lines with measured word caps instead.

Novelty and beginner: rotate K1's look by hold history in the MVP prompt. Deferred, not adopted: K1 no longer writes the question (a mid-read swap is a flicker), and one game of history is a coin flip; it is iteration two's headline, the question that remembers, with five games of log behind it.

Beginner: let the bot play on in every won position so he can deliver the mate. Partially rejected: it plays on only when it has king and pawns and he has a queen or rook; a thirty-move conversion against a bot with pieces does not fit his ten to fifteen minutes, and the stalemate hold covers the one failure that matters there.

Design: suppress K1 on the first hold of each session only. Went further: K1 is suppressed until the view has consented through Hear me out, because a dialog on the second hold is the same interruption as on the first.

Earlier spec (my own): the opponent 'plays like an 800'. Withdrawn as a claim and forbidden in copy; the opponent is described by what it does (takes everything you leave, leaves about two verified pieces a game) and by its measured results.
